signals.title: perf(test): move default test log level from `debug` to `info`
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Default test binaries to the `info` level rather than `debug`, in the test-only `init` of `pkg/util/log` that installs their logger. Make `comp/core/log/mock` follow that default instead of hardcoding it a second time, and have it restore the level that was actually in effect when a test ends, rather than assuming the default one. ### Motivation Every Go test binary in this repository logs at `debug`: the test-only `init` in `pkg/util/log` sets it, and `comp/core/log/mock` hardcoded it again for the 139 packages importing that mock. Once the level admits a line, it gets formatted, run through dozens of replacers of `pkg/util/scrubber` to redact credentials, then written out, through `t.Log` for the mock or stdout for the default logger. Tests that pass pay that too, `gotestsum` running `go test -json`, so none of it is dropped. Scrubbing one such line costs 15 allocations and about 7KiB. A run of `pkg/collector/corechecks/system/disk/diskv2` emits 9985 debug lines and one of `pkg/serverless/metrics` 4925, none of which survive this change. Both packages fail the 180s per-binary timeout of `tests_windows-x64`, at times ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1915978075)). ### Describe how you validated your changes Medians of 5 interleaved runs under CI's `-race` and `-covermode=atomic`: | package | before | after | | |---|---|---|---| | `pkg/collector/corechecks/system/disk/diskv2` | 23.13s | 15.50s | -33% | | `pkg/serverless/metrics` | 7.68s | 2.67s | -65% | Neither pair of distributions overlaps. The gain is ~4 times smaller on an uninstrumented build, -8% and -25%: the race detector and atomic coverage counters weigh more on an allocation-bound path than on a compute-bound one. `TestNewRestoresPreviousLogLevel` covers the restore, and fails against the assumed default. 419 tests pass across `comp/core/log` and `pkg/util/log`. ### Additional Notes `DD_LOG_LEVEL` keeps overriding the level, unchanged. A mock can put back the level but not the logger it replaced: `SetupLogger` closes whatever logger it supersedes.
signals.author: rdesgroppes

signals.title: perf(ebpf): declare eBPF headers per program, enforce with a build check
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? eBPF programs used to depend on monolithic `cc_library` targets that aggregated entire header trees (`ebpf_c_headers`, `ebpf_c_network`, `security_ebpf_headers`, …). Clang was therefore handed **2939 repo-owned headers it never opened**, and touching any header in a tree invalidated every program that pulled that tree in. Three changes: 1. **A new Gazelle extension** (`bazel/rules/ebpf_c/`) generates one `cc_library` per header (296 across 13 trees) and derives the `deps` of all 53 `ebpf_prog` / `ebpf_program_suite` targets from the `#include`s of their source. These `deps` are now generated — run `bazel run //:gazelle` after adding or removing an eBPF header. 2. **A validation action per program** fails the build when a declared header is never opened, so over-declared `deps` cannot come back. It reuses the `unused_inputs_list` machinery from #54349, which also prunes those headers from the action's inputs and so avoids needless recompilation. 3. **Config-conditional headers move into the rule**, because whether clang reads them depends on flags the rule sets rather than on anything visible in the build graph: `asm_goto_workaround.h` (force-included into prebuilt programs) and `vmlinux.h` (reachable only under `-DCOMPILE_CORE`). `vmlinux.h`'s architecture variant is chosen by a `select()` on the existing `target_arch` flag via the new `//pkg/ebpf/c:hdr/vmlinux_arch` target. Over-declared header edges go from 2939 to zero enforced. The 39 remaining entries are irreducible: an `#include` behind a disabled `#ifdef` is declared but never read. Those are recorded in a new `allowed_unused` attribute on the 20 affected targets, each with a comment naming the guard — `kconfig.h` under `COMPILE_RUNTIME`, security test headers under `__BALOUM__`, two TLS headers under `#ifndef COMPILE_PREBUILT`, and `offsets.h` under `COMPILE_PREBUILT`. Entries that become used again are reported as stale, so the list cannot rot. The monolithic libraries are **kept**: Go cgo test targets across `pkg/network/protocols/*` depend on them to share struct definitions, and the `*_files` filegroups feed the runtime-compilation bundles in `pkg/ebpf/bytecode`. Only three now-dead `_COMMON_DEPS` variables were removed. ### Motivation Two wins. Correctness: nothing is declared to clang without being read, and the build now enforces that rather than relying on review. Build performance: a header change no longer invalidates every program in its tree, since each program declares only what it includes. Tradeoffs worth calling out: - **`deps` of eBPF programs and all `hdr/*` libraries are now generated.** Editing them by hand is pointless; the next Gazelle run overwrites them. Documented in `bazel/AGENTS.md`. - **Two places must stay in sync**: `ruleOwnedIncludes` in the extension and the flags `ebpf.bzl` sets. Called out in a comment on both sides. - Headers that `#include` each other share one library, because Bazel rejects the cycle that C tolerates through include guards. Exactly one such cycle exists (`protocols/http/http.h` ↔ `protocols/tls/https.h`). - Per-header libraries deliberately live in the tree's **root** package with slash-bearing names (`//pkg/network/ebpf/c:hdr/protocols/tls/tags`). Giving subdirectories their own packages would require `strip_include_prefix`, whose `_virtual_includes` paths stop matching what clang writes into its depfile, silently disabling the check. ### Describe how you validated your changes - All **53 eBPF programs build green on both `aarch64` and `x86_64`**, with the validation action passing on both. Verified the arch `select()` with `cquery`: under `--//bazel/rules/ebpf:target_arch=x86_64` only `hdr/vmlinux_6_14_0` is declared and the arm variant is absent, with zero repo-owned vmlinux residual on either architecture. - Downstream consumers build: `//pkg/ebpf/bytecode/...`, `//pkg/network/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/gpu/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/dyninst/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/collector/corechecks/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/security/ebpf/...`, plus`//bazel/rules/ebpf:cgo_godefs_tests` (7/7 pass). - New unit test `//bazel/rules/ebpf:check_unused_inputs_test` covers the checker: kernel headers ignored, unused repo header rejected, allowance honoured, stale allowance rejected. - **Regeneration tested**: deleted a generated library and replaced a program's per-header deps with the old monolith; a single `bazel run //:gazelle` restored both byte-for-byte, including cross-tree edges. Hand-written `allowed_unused` and the `# keep` on `hdr/vmlinux_arch` survived. Gazelle and buildifier are idempotent. ### Additional Notes Builds on #54349 (`perf(ebpf): prune unused compile inputs`), which added the `unused_inputs_list` clang wrapper this PR's check depends on. CI is the first run of the validation action outside my container. If a runner's default `target_arch` produces a different conditional-include set than the two I tested, it would surface as an `allowed_unused` mismatch naming the exact target and header — the residual was identical on both architectures locally, so I do not expect this.
signals.author: JSGette

signals.title: [CWS] Host-wide capture window on the V2 security profile manager
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? V2 alternative to #53808. Same feature — a host-wide "start → run job → stop → collect local profiles" capture button for CI — but built on the **V2 security profile manager** instead of the V1 activity dump machinery, since V1 is being deprecated. - New CLI: `system-probe runtime activity-dump host start` / `host stop` (same surface as the V1 PR). - New config switch `runtime_security_config.security_profile.v2.host_dump.enabled` (default **false**), which also enables the V2 manager and host cgroup profiling (upward-only, logged) so a single switch works. - **Host coverage:** V2 currently drops every non-container event at the top of `ProcessEvent` ("Filter out systemd cgroups for now"). Under `host_dump` that filter is lifted, and `buildWorkloadSelector` keys host workloads on their cgroup `service` tag — one profile per systemd unit, matching the granularity of V1's host dumps. Tag-resolution readiness uses `service`/`version` for host workloads instead of `image_name`/`image_tag`. - **Local-only:** the remote storage request isn't registered when `host_dump` is on, so nothing is forwarded to the backend and the intake endpoints aren't set up. Loading previously persisted profiles from disk is also skipped, since it would resurrect a stale tree into a fresh window. - `ListActivityDumps` now reports the in-memory profiles under V2 (it was a no-op), giving the CLI a readiness/inspection view. - **Self-contained windows:** opening a window also flushes the kernel dedup sample maps (`open_samples`, `bind_samples`, `connect_samples`, `pid_path_keys`). Those are global LRUs keyed by `(process, target)` that know nothing about capture windows — the first open/connect for a key is delivered and later ones are discarded in kernel space, so without flushing, activity already touched before the window would stay invisible for its whole duration. This is userspace-only: the manager now receives the ebpf manager and deletes the entries; no eBPF C changes. If the maps can't be resolved the window still works, it just can't replay already-deduplicated activity. ### How the window maps onto V2 V1's button worked because a "dump" is a discrete object with a start/stop lifecycle. V2 has no such object: profiles are built continuously from the event stream, keyed by workload selector, and flushed on a ticker. So the window is re-expressed as: | | V1 | V2 (this PR) | |---|---|---| | `host start` | reset each dump's tree + snapshot all cgroups | discard all in-memory profiles, empty the tag-resolution queues, purge the sample-cookie LRU | | `host stop` | finalize + persist each dump | persist every profile recorded during the window | | scope | per-cgroup kernel gating (`traced_cgroups`) | no kernel gating at all; V2 consumes every event, so scope is a userspace filter | Concurrency: the profile set is snapshotted under `profilesLock` and encoding/disk writes happen after releasing it, so a slow disk cannot stall event ingestion (which needs the same lock to look up or create profiles). ### Motivation Spotting anomalous behaviour in CI jobs (ephemeral VM runners): a GitHub Action opens the window at job start and collects the per-workload profiles at job end. Keeping it local-only keeps the captured data on the box. V1 will be deprecated, so the capability needs to exist on V2. ### Describe how you validated your changes Built and validated end to end on a Linux dev VM running `system-probe` standalone, with a minimal config that sets **only** `security_profile.v2.host_dump.enabled: true` (plus a custom local output directory) so the run also exercises the prerequisite pull-up. **Auto-coupling** — startup logs from the single switch: ``` security_profile.v2.host_dump.enabled=true: enabling security_profile.v2.enabled security_profile.v2.host_dump.enabled=true: aligning security_profile.dir with activity_dump.local_storage.output_directory (...) ``` (the dir alignment is needed because `activity_dump.enabled` defaults to true, and enabling security profiles brings in the "both directories must match" constraint — without it the runtime security module refuses to start with a custom output directory) **Capture window**, running the activity directly on the host (not in a container): ``` $ activity-dump host start host-wide capture window started (25 previously recorded profiles discarded) $ id; whoami; cat /etc/passwd; nslookup google.com; wget example.com $ activity-dump host stop host-wide capture stopped, 2 profiles persisted: - cgroup ID: /user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-4.scope tags: service:session-4.scope - cgroup ID: /system.slice/systemd-resolved.service tags: service:systemd-resolved.service ``` Both `storage type: local_storage`. The 25 discarded profiles confirm host workloads are being profiled; the 2 persisted are exactly the cgroups active during the window (my shell session, and systemd-resolved which served the DNS) — per-systemd-unit granularity as intended. **Content of the host session profile** — every requested category is present: | Category | Captured | |---|---| | processes | `/usr/bin/id`, `/usr/bin/whoami`, `/usr/bin/cat`, `/usr/bin/nslookup`, `/usr/bin/wget`, `/usr/bin/zsh` | | files | `/etc/passwd` | | DNS | `google.com`, `example.com` | | connections | `AF_INET` socket nodes, bind address `0.0.0.0` | **Repeated cycles and dedup flushing** — the decisive test: run *identical* commands from the *same* parent shell in two consecutive windows, so the kernel dedup key `(ppid, exe, file)` is the same both times. Without the flush the second window would miss the repeated file open. ``` parent shell pid=28926 (identical for both windows) WINDOW A: host-wide capture window started (25 profiles discarded, 440 kernel dedup entries flushed) cat /etc/passwd; wget example.com -> 2 profiles persisted WINDOW B: host-wide capture window started (2 profiles discarded, 602 kernel dedup entries flushed) cat /etc/passwd; wget example.com -> 2 profiles persisted ``` Both windows contain `/etc/passwd`, `example.com` and the `cat`/`wget` execs, so a window is a complete record of what happened during it, not just of what was novel since boot. **Local-only** — `grep -c remote_storage` over the stop output returns `0`, and no cws-intake endpoint is set up at startup. **Unit tests** — 921/921 pass across `pkg/security/security_profile`, `pkg/security/config` and `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/runtime`, including new coverage for the prerequisite pull-up (enable + dir alignment), the off-is-noop case, and the `host start`/`host stop` CLI wiring. ### Additional Notes - **Draft.** Opening for early review of the approach. - Flushing the dedup maps on `host start` means the first events after a window opens are re-delivered rather than suppressed, so there is a brief cost in event volume at the start of each window. That is the intended trade for a self-contained capture. - Exceeding `security_profile.v2.max_dump_size` calls `Profile.Disable()`, which discards the whole tree — so an oversized host profile yields nothing rather than a truncated capture. Worth revisiting for host-wide use. - `host_dump` makes V2 fully local, so it cannot be combined with normal backend-forwarded profiling. - Supersedes #53808 in intent; that PR is left open for comparison.
signals.author: loresuso

signals.title: [ AGNTLOG-701 ] Support certificate revocation lists on TLS log listeners
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `crl_file` setting to the `tls` block of a TCP log listener. When client certificate verification is enabled, any client whose verified certificate chain contains a revoked certificate is turned away during the TLS handshake. The file may hold one or more certificate revocation lists in either PEM or DER form, and it is reloaded from disk on the same cadence as the CA bundle, so publishing an updated list takes effect without restarting the Agent. A revocation list is only applied to certificates issued by the CA that signed it: the list's issuer name must match the candidate issuer in the chain and its signature must verify against that issuer's key. An unrelated list left in the file, or one copied from the wrong PKI, therefore cannot lock out valid clients. Configuring `crl_file` without `client_auth` set to `optional` or `required` is rejected at config validation time rather than silently ignored, and a listener whose CRL file cannot be read refuses to start instead of degrading to no revocation checking. ### Motivation Client certificate verification previously had no way to turn away a certificate before its natural expiry. An operator whose client key was compromised had to either rotate the CA and reissue every client certificate, or wait out the remaining validity window. Revocation lists are the standard answer to that problem and are what a PKI team expects a TLS server to honor. Expired lists are still enforced rather than ignored, since refusing to apply a stale list would re-admit every certificate it revokes. A warning is logged when a loaded list is past its `nextUpdate` so a stalled CRL distribution is visible to the operator. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logs-library/utils/tls/...`, `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logs/agent/config` and `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/logs/launchers/listener` all pass. New coverage spans the three layers: revocation matching (revoked leaf, revoked intermediate, list signed by an impostor CA with a colliding subject name, cross-signed chains where only one path is revoked), list loading and hot reload (PEM, DER, concatenated lists from several issuers, reload failure preserving the previous lists), and config validation. End to end, `TestTCPMTLSRejectsRevokedClientCert` and `TestTCPMTLSAcceptsClientCertAbsentFromCRL` drive a real TLS handshake against the listener. The rejection test was checked against a deliberately broken build with revocation enforcement disabled: it fails there on both assertions, so it is not passing vacuously. It also distinguishes a server-side rejection from a read deadline, which would otherwise satisfy a naive error assertion. ### Additional Notes No release note is attached because TLS support on log listeners is not yet generally available.
signals.author: ddrthall

signals.title: [ AGNTLOG-702 ] Restrict TLS log listeners to named client identities
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds an `allowed_client_names` setting to the `tls` block of a TCP log listener. When set, a client must not only present a certificate the configured CA trusts, but that certificate must also carry an identity on the list. Entries are matched against every subject alternative name in the certificate — DNS, email, IP and URI — as well as the subject common name. Each identity is compared under the case rules of its own type, so nothing is matched more loosely than its syntax allows: DNS names, IP addresses and the common name ignore case, an email address folds only its domain and keeps its local part exact, and a URI must match exactly, since folding a URI path would let one SPIFFE workload identity authorize a different one. IP entries are compared in canonical form, so an uncompressed IPv6 address still matches the form a certificate presents. Wildcards are never interpreted: an entry containing one matches literally rather than quietly authorizing a whole domain. The setting requires `client_auth: required`; under `optional` a client can decline to send a certificate and would bypass the list entirely, so that combination is rejected at config validation time rather than accepted and ignored. When a client is turned away, the handshake failure logged by the listener names both the identities the certificate presented and the configured entries, so the mismatch can be diagnosed without reproducing the connection. ### Motivation Mutual TLS previously answered only "did the CA vouch for this client". Organizations commonly run one internal CA for a wide range of workloads, so trusting that CA on a log listener also trusts every certificate it has ever issued, including hosts with no business shipping logs. Operators coming from other syslog servers expect to be able to pin the specific senders they intend to accept. Common name matching is intentionally kept alongside subject alternative names, even though RFC 6125 hostname verification ignores the common name whenever any SAN is present. This is client authorization rather than server identity verification, and client certificates in the field routinely carry their identity only in the common name. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logs-library/utils/tls/...`, `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logs/agent/config` and `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/logs/launchers/listener` all pass. New coverage includes matching on each identity type, the per-type case rules, rejection of substring and wildcard near-misses, certificates carrying no identity at all, blank entries from a trailing comma in a comma-separated list, and the validation rules. End to end, `TestTCPMTLSAcceptsAllowedClientName`, `TestTCPMTLSRejectsUnlistedClientName` and `TestTCPMTLSAcceptsAnyClientWhenNoNamesConfigured` drive real TLS handshakes against the listener. The rejection test was checked against a deliberately broken build with the name check disabled: it fails there on both assertions, so it is not passing vacuously. It also distinguishes a server-side rejection from a read deadline, which would otherwise satisfy a naive error assertion. The two case-sensitivity rules were verified the same way, against a build that folded URIs and mail local parts. ### Additional Notes No release note is attached because TLS support on log listeners is not yet generally available. Wildcard and regular-expression entries were deliberately left out. They can be added later without breaking existing configuration, whereas retrofitting exact-match semantics onto entries that were previously treated as patterns could not be done safely.
signals.author: ddrthall

signals.title: apm: use url.template for OTLP HTTP client resource names
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Uses the OpenTelemetry `url.template` attribute when generating resource names for HTTP client spans. Client spans now use `METHOD url.template` when available and retain the method-only fallback otherwise. Server spans continue to use `METHOD http.route`. Fixes #31570. ## Motivation HTTP client resource names currently collapse to the HTTP method even when OpenTelemetry instrumentation provides a low-cardinality URL template. Using the template produces more useful resource grouping without falling back to high-cardinality raw URLs. ## Testing Added focused unit coverage for client URL templates, method-only fallback, and client/server attribute precedence. Local `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/api,./pkg/trace/otel/traceutil` could not run because Windows Defender quarantined the standalone `dda.exe` after its PyPI bootstrap failed with a TLS handshake error. CI is expected to run the required test targets. ## Additional Notes The current commit is unsigned because no local signing key is configured; it will need to be replaced with a signed commit before merge.
signals.author: niharikag09

signals.title: [WP] Read OTel thread local context records (OTEP 4947)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds support for reading span/trace IDs from native applications using the OpenTelemetry Thread Local Context Record format (OTel spec #4947) in the CWS eBPF security module. The implementation adds a new eBPF read path that: Discovers the OTel TLSDESC TLS variable offset (registered by user-space) Dereferences the TLS pointer to locate the OTel Thread Local Context Record This targets native applications using ELF TLSDESC (C, C++, Rust, Java/JNI, .NET/FFI, Python native extensions). ### Motivation The OpenTelemetry specification defines a standard mechanism for SDKs to publish thread-level trace context (trace ID, span ID) through ELF Thread Local Storage so that out-of-process readers like eBPF probes can correlate security events with distributed traces. Supporting this standard allows CWS to automatically pick up span context from any OTel-instrumented native application without requiring Datadog-specific instrumentation. ### Describe how you validated your changes * All modified Go packages (probe/erpc, probe/constantfetch, ebpf/probes, ptracer, probe) build cleanly * The C syscall tester compiles successfully with the new otel-span-open command * Added a functional test (TestOTelSpan) that: * Creates a __thread TLS variable in C, computes its offset from fsbase via arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_FS) * Registers the offset with eBPF via the new REGISTER_OTEL_TLS_OP eRPC operation * Fills an OTel Thread Local Context Record with a known trace ID and span ID in W3C byte order * Triggers an open() syscall and verifies the correct trace/span IDs appear in the captured security event ### Additional Notes
signals.author: danielmercier

signals.title: fix(remoteagentregistry): canonicalize local metric help
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes Core Agent telemetry HELP text canonical when Remote Agent Registry (RAR) merges incoming Prometheus telemetry. The telemetry component records HELP text for metric families it creates in the normal `/telemetry` registry. When RAR receives a remote family with the same name, it uses that local HELP text when constructing the forwarded Prometheus descriptor. Remote-only families retain the remote agent's HELP text. ### Motivation Prometheus requires metric families that share a name to use identical HELP text. A remote agent can currently supply a different description for a metric also emitted by Core Agent, causing the combined telemetry gather to fail. The Core Agent definition is the authoritative local contract. This includes the Core Agent DogStatsD client byte counters added in #54381. The regression coverage verifies that Core Agent's `dogstatsd_client__bytes_sent` HELP wins over incompatible ADP text while retaining the ADP sample and authoritative `emitter` label. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/telemetry/impl:impl_test //comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl:impl_test --test_output=errors` - `git diff --check` - Independent spec-compliance and code-quality reviews. `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` and `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` were blocked before compilation by an internal dependency-mirror HTTP 403 for `github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/extension/healthcheckextension@v0.158.0`, which is in its mirror cooldown window. ### Additional Notes The canonical HELP catalog deliberately covers metrics created through the telemetry component's counter, gauge, and histogram factory APIs. It excludes `DefaultMetric` and opaque direct `RegisterCollector` registrations, which are not part of RAR's normal telemetry registry merge path.
signals.author: thieman

signals.title: [ACTP] package and activate par-control
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Packages and activates split-mode PAR on Linux and Windows hosts: - installs `par-control` and process-manager definitions for it and the on-demand executor; - adds Agent package, installer, and Windows executable-resource wiring; - preserves a standard Unix service `PATH` for process-manager children; - adds fake-OPMS support plus Linux and Windows lifecycle/bootstrap E2E suites and CI jobs. Two details about how the definitions delegate to `dd-procmgrd`: - Windows has no console for a service to inherit, so the `par-control` definition redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `<ETC_ROOT>/logs/par-control.log` instead of the binary managing its own log file. `dd-procmgrd` now creates a missing stdio parent directory rather than silently falling back to inherit on a fresh install. - The PAR definitions set `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR=${DD_CONF_DIR}/managed/datadog-agent/stable`, which `dd-procmgrd` expands from the supervising unit, so a stable or experiment unit selects the matching config tree. Hardcoding the rendered stable path would have made the control plane and executor read stable policies during an experiment while the core Agent read the experiment's. This matches what the DDOT definition already does. Windows keeps reading `fleet_policies_dir` from the registry, as `pkg/config/setup/config_windows.go` does, because there are no experiment services there. Docker and Kubernetes deployments remain monolithic. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages:packages_test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:tmpl_test //pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test` - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/privateactionrunner` The installer test now pins the full `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` value for both definitions; asserting only the key name would not catch a regression to a hardcoded path. Live Linux and Windows E2E execution is left to CI. _Stack 9 of 9; based on #54594._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [SVLS-9526] Enhance startup diagnostics and surface image version
signals.text: ## Summary Stacks on #54537. When `DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`, emit a structured block at startup covering everything needed to debug serverless-init across all cloud platforms: - **`serverless_init_version`** — Docker image tag injected at build time via `-ldflags` (`pkg/serverless/tags.currentExtensionVersion`). Makes the 1:1 mapping between image tag and agent version explicit in logs. - **`deployment_model`** — `sidecar` or `init-container` - **`wrapped_command`** — the command serverless-init is wrapping, if any - **`uuid (agent)`** — the gopsutil UUID that `inventoryagent` sends to Subotka, with a direct REDAPL query hint - **Inventory pipeline section** — `first_run_delay`, `min/max interval`, `enable_metadata_collection` — confirms `ForceCollect()` preconditions at a glance - **Env var block** — all env vars (secrets masked) for platform debugging ## Changes - `cmd/serverless-init/mode/mode.go` — add `DeploymentModel` + `WrappedCommand` fields to `Conf` - `cmd/serverless-init/diagnostic/diagnostic.go` — new package with structured startup log block - `cmd/serverless-init/diagnostic/diagnostic_test.go` — unit tests ## Test plan - [ ] Set `DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`, trigger cold start — confirm all fields appear in logs - [ ] Confirm `serverless_init_version` reads `xxx` for branch builds (overridden to real tag by `serverless-init-ci` ldflags) - [ ] `dda inv test --targets=./cmd/serverless-init/...`
signals.author: nina9753

signals.title: [SVLS-9526] Add serverless-init inventory fields for serverless_init_agent table
signals.text: ## Summary - Adds `cmd/serverless-init/inventory` package that populates serverless-specific metadata fields in the `inventoryagent` component before `ForceCollect()` is called at container startup - Fields prefixed `serverless_` feed the `serverless_init_agent` REDAPL table via the agentmetadata EPRW decoder ([SVLS-9607](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9607)) - Schema defined in [SVLS-9604](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9604), dd-source table PR already created ## Context Serverless-init containers scale to zero in seconds. The `datadog_agent` table uses hostname-based entity resolution, but serverless-init always reports `hostname=""`, so no rows land in Fleet. The fix (PR #54537) added `ForceCollect()` to guarantee one payload is sent per cold start. This PR adds the payload content that routes to the new `serverless_init_agent` table. ## Fields collected All fields confirmed available across 9 platform test deployments (SVLS-9526 diagnostic data): | Field | Source | Notes | |---|---|---| | `serverless_cloud_provider` | derived from origin | `gcp` / `azure` | | `serverless_workload_type` | derived from origin | `cloud_run_service`, `cloud_run_function`, `cloud_run_job`, `container_app`, `app_service` | | `serverless_origin` | `cloudService.GetOrigin()` | raw: `cloudrun`, `cloudrunjobs`, `containerapp`, `appservice` | | `serverless_resource_name` | platform env var | `K_SERVICE` / `CONTAINER_APP_NAME` / `WEBSITE_SITE_NAME` | | `serverless_deployment_model` | `mode.Conf.SidecarMode` | `sidecar` / `init-container` | | `serverless_agent_commit` | `-ldflags` build-time inject | commit SHA | | `serverless_runtime` | base-image env vars | `python3.11.x`, `node20.x`, etc. | | `serverless_wrapped_command` | `os.Args[1:]` | init-container only | | `serverless_dd_site` / `logs_enabled` / `apm_enabled` | agent config | | | `serverless_dd_env` / `dd_service` / `dd_version` | DD_* env vars | omitted if not set | | `serverless_subscription_id` / `resource_group` | Azure env vars | Azure only | | `serverless_tracer_version` | `DD_TRACE_VERSION` | usually absent | ## Stacks on - PR #54537 (`svls-9526/force-collect`) — `ForceCollect()` implementation - PR #54538 (`svls-9526/diagnostic-v2`) — diagnostic enhancements ## Test plan - [ ] Unit tests pass: `go test -tags "serverless otlp" ./cmd/serverless-init/inventory/...` - [ ] Build passes: `go build -tags "serverless otlp" ./cmd/serverless-init/...` - [ ] Manual: deploy serverless-init with `DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true` and verify `serverless_*` fields appear in `SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC` output in logs (they are set via `ia.Set()` which logs at debug level) - [ ] Integration: wait for SVLS-9607 (EPRW decoder) and verify rows appear in `serverless_init_agent` REDAPL table [SVLS-9607]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9607?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [SVLS-9604]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9604?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: Group CWS functional tests by module config
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the CWS functional suite run as one `go test` pass per module config instead of one pass for everything. A test declares the static config it needs next to the test function: ```go var _ = declare(TestDNSResolver, testOpts{networkIngressEnabled: true}) ``` Declaring nothing means the default config, which covers most of the suite and shares a single pass — so ~180 call sites are untouched. A config that is only knowable at run time (a `t.TempDir()`, a `which(t, "sleep")`, a callback) is still passed to `newTestModule` directly, and `declareInlineConfig` records that the test builds its own module. Because declarations register at `init()`, the partition is computable without running a test. The suite prints it as JSON with `-list-groups`, and the KMT test runner (`test/new-e2e/system-probe/test-runner`) runs one `gotestsum` pass per group, each with its own junit/testjson suffix and `-test.timeout`. Everything degrades to today's single unfiltered pass — a suite that predates the flag, output that does not parse, or a package the job already narrows with `-test.run`/`-test.skip` (`cws_ad`, `cws_peds`, `cws_req`). ### Motivation `newTestModule` rebuilds the eBPF manager whenever a test's static config differs from the live module's, at seconds to tens of seconds per rebuild (measured 34s teardown on `amazon_6.12`, 7s on 5.15). Only ~16 distinct configs exist, but the tests using them are scattered through source order, so an isolated non-default test costs two rebuilds — switch in, switch back. `cws_host` does **43** rebuilds today; the partition predicts **33** on that job. ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control resolved configuration
signals.text: ## this is in draft again, i'm investigating reusing saluki ### What does this PR do? Adds configuration and identity bootstrap for `par-control`. The reason this is a big PR is because some config loading behavior had to be adapted from Go to Rust. `par-control` now resolves agent and PAR config in _mostly_ the same way as the Go config loader. On startup it runs the new Go `ensure-enrollment` command (#54870) to detect or perform enrollment, then loads the identity. Note that unlike in the Go config loader, unresolved `ENC[...]` secrets are rejected. We did not (yet) implement the Agent secret-backend protocol or FIPS configuration transforms to lower the scope of this work. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo test -p par-control` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy -p par-control --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 4 of 9; based on #54870 and followed by #54591._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control executor channel
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated local gRPC channel between `par-control` and the Go executor: - health and readiness checks; - workflow signing-key synchronization that keeps the executor alive while synchronization is in progress without counting it as an active action. The executor's idle tracking gains a distinct activity counter for this, so non-action work suppresses idle exit while `ActiveActions` still reports only running actions; - action dispatch and terminal outcomes; - Unix-socket and Windows named-pipe transports using the Agent IPC certificate; - message limits sized for large action payloads. This layer introduces the crate's generated-bindings module and the local transport helpers, since it is the first one that needs executor protos and mTLS. OPMS polling and orchestration remain in later layers. ### Validation Focused Go and Rust tests cover the protocol, key synchronization and idle interaction, transport, and message limits. Proto changes are Bazel-validated because Cargo and Bazel use separate generated bindings. - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test //pkg/privateactionrunner/executor:executor_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo test -p par-control` _Stack 5 of 9; based on #54590 and followed by #54592._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control OPMS client
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated OPMS client for `par-control`: - ES256 runner JWT signing; - task dequeue, heartbeat, and terminal publication; - runner health checks; - proxy, TLS, retry, and wire behavior matching the Go runner. Orchestration policy remains in the next layer. ### Validation Rust unit and HTTP/TLS contract tests cover request signing, payloads, pacing, proxying, and TLS behavior. Native TLS coverage runs on Linux and Windows. _Stack 6 of 9; based on #54591 and followed by #54593._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Executor idle shutdown is self-owned by the Go executor rather than driven by `par-control` process-manager calls. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] wire split runner ownership
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the monolithic Go runner stand down when split mode is enabled on supported Linux and Windows host installations. Containers and unsupported platforms keep the monolithic runner because they do not yet launch the complete replacement topology. This preserves the invariant that exactly one runner polls OPMS without disabling the only available runner. ### Validation - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` Tests cover Linux and Windows hosts, containers, and unsupported platforms. _Stack 8 of 9; based on #54593 and followed by #54529._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded by a single gate: **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. Every `unshare` call is reported once that gate opens, so all 12 exposed `CLONE_*` constants are matchable and the `flags` field carries the full raw bitmask. An earlier revision also filtered kernel-side on `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. That was dropped in review: it silently made rules on the other exposed constants (`CLONE_NEWUTS`, `CLONE_NEWIPC`, `CLONE_NEWTIME`, …) unable to fire. Per-flag volume control belongs in `unshare` approvers, as a follow-up. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of the gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: fix(e2e): retry ensure-adws-started on transient SSH/script failures
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds an onError resource hook that retries the ensure-adws-started command when sshd dies mid-command or the command's own PowerShell errors out, without retrying dial-exhaustion failures or the whole stack up. ### Motivation ensure-adws-started fails flakily shortly after domain-controller promotion (WINA-2095) due to transient SSH/script issues that a retry fixes. Requires the CI Pulumi CLI/engine to be bumped to >= v3.219.0 for onError hook support (tracked separately). ### Describe how you validated your changes Windows e2e tests should pass.
signals.author: clarkb7

signals.title: [procmgr] Windows spawn profiles foundation
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Introduces **Windows spawn profiles** in dd-procmgr so managed children can run under different security contexts: - **Privileged**: spawn as LocalSystem (supervisor primary token) - **AgentUser**: spawn as the agent service account (`ddagentuser`) Adds the Windows spawn stack (token logon, user profile load, supervision job, suspended `CreateProcessAsUserW`), a **privileged spawn catalog** that rejects unexpected command/args/env for privileged children, and **gRPC named-pipe caller authentication** for mutating RPCs. Also refactors the daemon runtime into a **`Supervisor` event loop** plus `ProcessManager` handlers, and runs **dd-procmgr-service as LocalSystem** so agent-profile spawn can read the agent password from LSA. **Stack context (PR 1):** | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | This PR | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on this PR; not on the merge spine) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | **Explicitly deferred:** config gates (#54732), secret-backend cache invalidation (#54734), process-agent dual-mode (#54735), full `ReloadConfig` (#55080). RPC/CLI for reload stay in this PR but return `UNIMPLEMENTED` until #55080. ### Motivation Process-agent on Windows must run as LocalSystem; other agent children should stay on the agent user. Spawn profiles make that explicit and enforceable at spawn time, and are a prerequisite for moving process-agent supervision off legacy SCM in #54735. LocalSystem MSI lands here so agent-profile children (ADP, PAR, DDOT) can spawn without waiting for #54735. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Bazel/Cargo procmgr Rust unit tests (Linux + Windows CI) - Privileged spawn catalog and spawn-profile unit tests (`pkg/procmgr/rust/...`) - COAT package tests (`pkg/procmgr/coat/...`) - Windows new-e2e: ADP, PAR, DDOT running tests, plus LocalSystem / agent-user identity checks (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-runtimes/procmgr/`) ### Additional Notes - **Fleet:** DDOT extension uninstall uses `ReloadOrRestartProcmgr()` (reload stub → SCM restart fallback). No process-agent dual-mode changes in this PR. - **ReloadConfig:** Proto and `dd-procmgr reload` remain for API compatibility; handler returns `UNIMPLEMENTED` until [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). - Supersedes the spawn portion of [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249).
signals.author: jose-manuel-almaza

signals.title: [procmgr] Config gates for processes.d auto-start
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds **config gates** to dd-procmgr so `processes.d` definitions can use `condition_config_any` to auto-start only when Agent config says they should. Implementation mirrors the Windows legacy SCM startup checks in `dependent_services_windows.go` and Agent config resolution: - YAML lookup (case-insensitive keys, flattened dotted keys, permissive parse fallback, merge keys) - Environment bindings (`DD_*`) with Agent precedence (ignore empty values, no trim before `ParseBool`, legacy `process_config.enabled` transforms) - Fleet policy merge - Derived `system_probe_config.enabled` (USM/NPM/security knobs, sk-tracer and discovery adjustments) - Windows: read `DD_*` overrides from the core Agent SCM `Environment` registry when not set in the procmgr process env Wires gate evaluation into `ManagedProcess` start/reload paths in the manager. **Stack context:** PR 2. Builds on [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) (`jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles`). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | This PR | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation Moving subservices (starting with process-agent) to dd-procmgr requires the supervisor to apply the same start/stop rules as the Agent today. Without config gates, a `processes.d` entry would always spawn when registered, which breaks parity with legacy SCM and fleet policy. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/` (env bindings, YAML load, system-probe derivations, gate evaluation) - Go unit tests for Windows config helpers (`pkg/config/setup/config_windows_test.go`) - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI ### Additional Notes - No `ENC[...]` / secret backend resolution in this PR (fleet policy `ENC[...]` values are not resolved here either). - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Schema comment sync in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/process_config.yaml` for env binding documentation. - Small exports in `pkg/system-probe/config/` so procmgr gate derivations stay aligned with Go `adjust*` logic.
signals.author: jose-manuel-almaza

signals.title: [procmgr] Secret backend resolution for config gates
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Resolves `ENC[...]` values during config gate evaluation so dd-procmgr matches Agent secret handling. Adds: - `config_gate/secrets.rs`: resolve handles via `secret_backend_command`, native `secret_backend_type`, and `multi_secret_backends` (same precedence as the core Agent) - Platform secret backend runners (Windows `CreateProcessAsUserW` under the Agent account; Unix setuid when procmgr runs as root for Privileged children) - `secret_backend_exec.rs`: shared spawn, timeout, stdout drain, and response parsing - Windows ACL validation on secret backend executables before spawn - Agent config precedence for backend settings: `DD_SECRET_BACKEND_*` env (including core Agent SCM `Environment` on Windows) over `datadog.yaml` - Manager reload: invalidate secret caches when config changes Fleet policy `ENC[...]` values stay unresolved here, matching Agent `MergeFleetPolicy` running after secret resolution. **Stack context:** PR 3. Builds on [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) (`jose/procmgr-config-gates`). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | This PR | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation PR 2 config gates read YAML, env, and fleet policy, but many customers gate features with secret-backed settings (`ENC[api_key]`, secret-backed booleans, etc.). Without secret resolution, gates would mis-evaluate and auto-start behavior would diverge from the Agent. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/secrets.rs` and config gate integration tests (serialized env to avoid cross-test leakage) - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI - Linux CI: secret-backend tests run under the agent service user where required ### Additional Notes - Secret backends always run as the core Agent service account, not as the procmgr supervisor (LocalSystem) or a Privileged managed child. - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Invokes `secret-generic-connector` when no custom `secret_backend_command` is configured.

signals.title: [procmgr] Supervise process-agent on Windows via dd-procmgr
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Moves Windows **process-agent** supervision to **dd-procmgr** using the same dual-mode pattern as PAR: - Fleet installer writes `processes.d/datadog-agent-process.yaml` (Privileged spawn profile) - Legacy `datadog-process-agent` SCM service is suppressed when procmgr owns process-agent - Agent startup waits on `dd-procmgr-service` before starting gated legacy children; independent services (sysprobe, security-agent, installer) start without blocking on procmgr **Stack context:** PR 4. Builds on [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) → [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) → [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. Reload lands in [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | This PR | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation We want subservices on dd-procmgr instead of SCM. Process-agent needs LocalSystem on Windows; other agent children should stay on the agent user. This PR wires the product integration once the procmgr foundation (PRs 1–3) is in place. `dd-procmgr-service` already runs as LocalSystem from [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Go unit tests for dependent Windows service startup (`dependent_services_windows_test.go`) - Go unit tests for fleet installer templates and YAML path substitution (`processmanager/...`) - New Windows E2E: process-agent supervised by procmgr, runs as LocalSystem, legacy SCM stopped ### Additional Notes - Linux process-agent stays on systemd for now. Legacy SCM service registration is not removed yet. - Process-agent `processes.d` config uses the shared `install_root` helper (same as PAR/ADP). MSI `RemoveFolderEx` handles uninstall/rollback cleanup; no per-file MSI rollback custom actions. - Includes release note `windows-process-procmgr-dual-mode-b7d2e4a1c8f03962.yaml`. - Closes/supersedes [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249) once the full stack merges.

signals.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signals.title: WIF-48: wire delegated auth into endpoint subsystems
signals.text: ## Summary Stacked on #53517. That PR taught the `delegatedauth` component to write a resolved API key back into an `additional_endpoints` config slot. This PR makes the Agent's endpoint consumers understand the `DELA(...)` placeholder that sits in that slot until it resolves. A directive looks like `DELA(<org_uuid>, aws[, region=…, fallback=…])` and goes where an API key normally goes. Two things have to happen: nobody may ship it upstream as a literal key, and every affected subsystem has to keep a live watcher so the real key lands without a restart. ``` datadog.yaml pkg/config/setup comp/core/delegatedauth additional_endpoints: ──▶ scan 38 settings ──▶ AddInstance(org, provider) host: [DELA(org,aws)] (12 map + 26 list shape) exchange AWS proof → API key one instance per directive │ ▼ write key back into the SAME config slot (SourceSecret) │ ┌───────────────────────────────────────┘ ▼ config OnUpdate fires ┌───────────┬───────────┬───────────┬───────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ forwarder logs process orchestrator trace-agent (resolver) (endpoints) (endpoints) (endpoints) proxies + writers rebuild ``` Until a directive resolves, each consumer contributes **no** key for that endpoint rather than an empty or literal one, so no unauthenticated request is made — but the domain stays registered so the resolved key has somewhere to land. ## What changed | Area | Change | |---|---| | `pkg/config/setup` | Discovery: scans all 38 `*additional_endpoints` settings (12 map-shape, 26 list-shape), parses each directive, registers one delegated-auth instance per match. Fallback keys resolve through the secrets backend and are redacted in logs. | | `comp/forwarder/.../resolver` | Carries `HasPendingDelegatedAuth` so a pending-only domain stays usable and keeps its config watcher instead of being dropped at startup. | | `comp/logs/agent/config` | Pending directive → empty key + endpoint marked unreliable (a reliable destination with no key wedges the pipeline). Key updates live via the existing rotation callback. | | `pkg/process`, `pkg/orchestrator` | Same pending-key handling on their endpoint loaders. | | `pkg/trace/api` | Four proxy paths (`evp_proxy`, `openlineage`, `profiles`, `transports`) skip pending directives. `debugger`/`symdb` are covered via the shared transport. | | `comp/trace/config`, `pkg/trace/writer` | `additional_endpoints` reload rebuilds proxy transports **and** writer senders at runtime — no restart needed. | `pkg/trace` is vendored by the OTel Collector distro, so its `DELA(` check is a 3-line local helper (`pkg/trace/api/dela.go`) rather than an import of `pkg/config/utils`, which would have pulled `pkg/config/setup` into that module's graph. ## Known limitations - **`apm_config.telemetry.additional_endpoints` does not reload.** `NewTelemetryForwarder` snapshots its endpoints at construction and exposes no rebuild path, so a key resolving there needs a restart. Everything else reloads live. - **A logs endpoint that starts pending stays on the best-effort path** for the process lifetime. The pipelines partition reliable/unreliable destinations once at startup, so this can't be restored later; the key itself still updates live, so the endpoint does deliver. ## Testing 92% of the lines this PR adds are covered (`bazel coverage`, measured against the added lines specifically). Uncovered remainder is mostly error paths in the discovery layer. Regression tests worth calling out: - `pkg/trace/writer` — `RebuildSenders` swaps the sender slice and then closes the old senders' queues. `sender.Push` checks `closed` and sends as two separate steps, so a push overlapping a rebuild is a send-on-closed-channel panic. The writers hold `sendersMu` across the whole send to prevent it. The window is a few instructions wide and doesn't reproduce under stress, and timing can't distinguish the two implementations, so the tests observe the lock directly with `TryLock` while a send is in flight. - `pkg/process/util/api/config` — a pending endpoint must contribute an empty key list, not `[""]`; `DedupAPIKeys` doesn't filter empty strings, so `[""]` would reach the forwarder's authorizers as a literal `DD-Api-Key: ` header. - `pkg/trace/agent` — compile-time assertions pin the writer types against `RebuildAdditionalEndpointSenders`' structural type assertions, which would otherwise silently no-op if a writer stopped implementing `RebuildSenders`. `//comp/trace/config/impl:impl_test` fails locally only in `TestConfigHostname/external/*`, which needs a `go` binary in the Bazel sandbox. `//pkg/process/runner:runner_test` is platform-skipped on macOS. ## Release note The customer-facing note lives in #53517. Its current text says no subsystem reads `DELA(...)` directives yet — that stops being true when this PR lands, so the note needs updating there (or a new one here) before either merges. ## Dependency Depends on #53517.
