signals.title: feat(notableevents): add macOS shutdown-cause notable event
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a macOS notable event that reports **why the previous boot ended**, recovered after the fact from the PMU rather than observed live. On Apple silicon, PMU/PMIC driver services publish an `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` IORegistry property: an array of short ASCII tokens naming the fault conditions that preceded the last power-off. This PR reads that property, classifies the tokens, and emits one notable event per boot when the classification is a fault. Five fault classes are covered, spanning the whole dictionary of 80 known tokens — 59 of which are faults: | Class | Title | Tokens | Example families | | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | | `thermal` | macOS overheated shutdown | 14 | `ot`, `sochot`, `ntc_shdn` | | `power` | macOS power fault shutdown | 29 | `uv`, `ov`, `oc`, `buck`, `pgood` | | `crash` | macOS crash shutdown | 6 | `crash` | | `watchdog` | macOS watchdog timeout shutdown | 5 | `timeout` | | `hardware` | macOS hardware fault shutdown | 5 | `spmi`, `sgpio`, `fault`, `otp_crc` | - **Native reader** (`shutdown_cause_iokit_darwin.{c,h}`) walks the IOService plane, flattens every `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` array into a single `0x1f`-separated token sequence, and dedups as it writes — so no Core Foundation type crosses the cgo boundary. The whole plane is walked rather than matching a class because the publishing class is PMIC-specific and varies by Mac model, and IOKit cannot match on a property key alone (`kIOPropertyMatchKey` matches key *and* value). - **Classifier** (`shutdown_classify_darwin.go`) maps a token to its *family* (prefix before the first comma, a declared underscore family, or the whole token) and the family to one of five classes, resolved by fixed precedence: **thermal → power → crash → watchdog → hardware**. Thermal wins deliberately: a machine collapsing from heat also asserts reset, crash and power lines, and the event that matters most must not be titled as a crash. - **Event shape** (`format_darwin.go`) — `EventType` is the constant `"System shutdown fault"` so consumers can filter shutdown causes on one value; the class varies the title and message only. The payload reports every token observed *plus* the families and the fault subset the classifier acted on, so a reader sees both the raw evidence and what the verdict was based on: ```json "macos_shutdown_cause": { "source": "IOPMUBootFaultInfo", "classification": "thermal", "primary_family": "ot", "families": ["ot", "sochot"], "tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "fault_tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "boot_uuid": "…", "boot_time": "2026-08-11T09:55:21Z" } ``` - **Dedup is boot-scoped.** Identity is `shutdown:<bootUUID>:<sortedFaultTokens>`, hashed under a new `macos-shutdown-v1:` event-ID prefix. Both halves are load-bearing: the boot UUID alone says nothing about *what* was read, and the token set alone is identical across boots — a Mac that overheats every afternoon would emit one ID forever and be deduplicated into silence. Tokens are sorted first because PMU enumeration order is not stable (measured: two triggers with an identical fault set reported the groups in different order). - **Storage.** A new `ShutdownCause` bookmark field records the examined boot *whether or not* an event was emitted, so a cleanly-rebooting Mac does not re-read the property on every Agent restart. It is the primary guard rather than the `Acknowledged` map, which prunes after 30 days or 4096 entries — a Mac up longer than that would otherwise re-emit. The check runs **once per collector lifetime**, before the first directory scan, and is retried from the reconcile tick when it could not commit. It reads the property as an ordinary user (no root needed; system-probe runs as root regardless), and the whole feature is gated behind the existing `notable_events.enabled` setting, which defaults to `false`. **No benchmarks, deliberately.** There is no steady-state cost to measure: the IOService walk happens once per collector lifetime, is bounded at 16 services, and short-circuits as soon as every distinct token is accounted for. It is not on any per-event, per-scan or per-tick path. **Bookmark schema version stays at 1, deliberately.** `Load()` and `validateDarwinBookmarkState()` both require exact equality, so bumping to `2` would fail every existing v1 bookmark as corrupt — which resets state and re-baselines, discarding pending undelivered crash events on every upgraded host. `ShutdownCause` is `omitempty` with a nil zero value, so v1 bookmarks deserialize with no migration. Relatedly, `types.IsEventID()` had to learn the new prefix in the same change: a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID written under the old single-prefix check would fail validation on the next `Load()` and wipe the bookmark, silently losing every pending crash event. ### Motivation [https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040) **A hard shutdown kills the Agent before it can report why.** Whether the machine overheated, lost a power rail, asserted its CRASH line, tripped a watchdog or hit a hardware fault, the Agent is gone before it can say so — the cause has to be recovered from the PMU on the next boot, or it is never recovered at all. All five fault classes are in scope here; thermal is one of them, not the point of the feature. **Predecessor: macOS app crash notable events (#54084).** This builds directly on it, reusing its bookmark, its `Pending`/`Ack` delivery contract and its at-least-once semantics unchanged — a second event *source* on that pipeline, not a second pipeline. It complements rather than replaces it: #54084 reports `.ips` files, which are written by a *running* OS about a *running* process, so a PMU-forced power cut leaves no `.ips` at all. The one adjacent artifact that does exist, `.shutdownStall` spindumps, records a *stalled* shutdown, not its cause. Everything else was surveyed and rejected: `pmset -g log` carries no cause data (25,117 lines grepped, nothing), `nvram -p` has no shutdown-cause variable, `ioreg -rc IOPMrootDomain` has no such property, `last -x reboot` is empty, and the `AppleSMC: Previous shutdown cause: <N>` unified-log line that Intel Macs emit **does not exist on Apple silicon**. Without this, a machine that overheated or lost a power rail badly enough to be cut off is a silent gap in the fleet record. `kern.shutdownreason` is **deliberately not read** — not as a source, not as a fallback, not as payload. It is the same PMU data flattened into an 80-byte-capped string, and it was already destroying data on an ordinary clean shutdown of the test machine: the cap was hit in 4 of 6 measured boots, always cutting *mid-token* and synthesising fault names that do not exist (`crash,crash`, `btn_rst,btn`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_d`). Absence of a token from that sysctl carries no information at all. The tradeoff is accepted and known: the sysctl also carries application-processor tokens (`ap_restart`, `ap_panic`) that `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not, and this PR gives those up rather than add a second parsing path and a second failure mode. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests — 240 tests pass in `pkg/notableevents`** (verified locally on the branch head with `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/notableevents/...`). Classifier tests deliberately use **payloads measured from real hardware** as fixtures rather than invented ones: | Pattern | Tokens (distinct union) | Emits | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | A — clean shutdown | `target_off_restart`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | B — `sudo reboot` | `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | C — button/force restart | + `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `crash,crash0_in` | `crash`, `fault_tokens = ["crash,crash0_in"]` | Also covered: the full 80-token dictionary maps to exactly one family each with the asserted **59 fault / 21 benign** split (14 thermal, 29 power, 6 crash, 5 watchdog, 5 hardware) — this pins a typo in the family map that would otherwise silently misclassify; class precedence in every pairing; unknown *suffix* within a known family (`ot,some_future_sensor`) still classifies thermal, which is the prefix contract; permuted group order yields an identical event ID; benign-token exclusions are dead-weight-free (each is in the measured dictionary *and* would otherwise be a fault); every classification fits the wire limit; malformed and oversized payloads are rejected. Collector tests cover the delivery contract end to end: one event per boot; `Start()` → `Close()` → `Start()` yields one event, not two; same boot UUID after Ack yields nothing; a *different* boot UUID with the same tokens yields a new event; a saturated pending queue **defers** rather than records, because recording the boot would be final and the fault cannot be reproduced by a later boot; a `Save` failure leaves nothing pending and is retried; a check blocked by an in-flight bookmark commit is retried from the reconcile tick rather than stranded for the process lifetime; reader failure, absent property and untrusted payload all leave crash-report collection unaffected; a v1 bookmark with no `shutdown_cause` key loads without being treated as corrupt. **Manual QA on real hardware.** `Mac17,9` / M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), SIP enabled, no `boot-args`. **Six real boot sessions** executed one trigger at a time — the property is destroyed by the next reboot, so the runs could not be batched — with an immediate capture script per boot: `sudo reboot`, Control-Command-Power force restart, power button held ~10s, a deliberately stalled shutdown ended by the power button, the same stall resolved via Try Again → Force Quit, and a battery run-down. Three distinct payloads were observed across six distinct boot UUIDs, verified byte-identical by MD5, reverting to pattern A after a clean shutdown. That establishes the load-bearing premise: **the property is a live, event-driven, self-clearing signal, not a constant** — which is what validates both the read path and the boot-UUID dedup key. **How to reproduce a fault event yourself — the `crash` class, on demand.** One fault class is reproducible at will on Apple silicon, so a reviewer can exercise the whole path end to end without waiting for real hardware trouble. A force restart asserts the AP's CRASH line, which emits `crash,crash0_in`: 1. Enable the feature — it is off by default: ```bash # datadog.yaml notable_events: enabled: true ``` 2. Clear any prior bookmark so the check is not skipped as already-examined, and note that the file is root-owned: ```bash sudo rm -f /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json ``` 3. Record the current boot identity and the pre-restart payload, for comparison: ```bash sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo ``` 4. Force restart: hold **Control-Command-Power** until the screen blanks. (Holding the power button ~10s, or ending a stalled shutdown with the power button, both produce the same payload — see the resolution caveat in Additional Notes.) 5. After the machine boots, confirm the PMU now reports the crash token. Expect pattern C — `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `target_off_restart`, `crash,crash0_in`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert`: ```bash ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid # must differ from step 3 ``` 6. Start the Agent and system-probe, and confirm the event: ```bash sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.agent sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.sysprobe sudo cat /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json | jq . ``` Expect a `shutdown_cause` object whose `boot_uuid` matches step 5, and a `pending` entry with a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID, `"event_type": "System shutdown fault"`, title `macOS crash shutdown`, `"classification": "crash"`, and `fault_tokens` of exactly `["crash,crash0_in"]` — all six tokens appear in `tokens`, but only the crash one elected the class. 7. Confirm the dedup guard: restart the Agent without rebooting. No second event should be emitted, and `shutdown_cause.boot_uuid` should be unchanged. To verify the **negative** case, `sudo reboot` instead of step 4 (pattern B) or shut down cleanly from the Apple menu (pattern A). Both must produce a `shutdown_cause` record with **no** event — a clean shutdown emitting an event is the failure mode most worth catching, since `wdog,reset_in_1` is present on every ordinary shutdown. **`qa/rc-required` — why this needs RC validation.** The classes that matter most in the field cannot be triggered on any machine we control, and cannot be simulated at all: the property is written by the PMU at power-off and is read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store. Reproducing a genuine thermal, power-rail or hardware fault means real failing hardware. Virtualized macOS runners expose no PMU, so the property is simply absent there and CI can only assert graceful degradation. What RC deployment adds is a full end-to-end test on real hardware: that the notable event is actually emitted and delivered, and that its tags and payload arrive intact. The predecessor, #54084, carried the same label for the same reason. **What was NOT validated, and cannot be:** - **No thermal token has ever been observed on this machine** — not `ot,*`, not `sochot,*`, not `ntc_shdn`. The thermal classification is inferred from token names in the PMU's own declared dictionary (published as `info-fault_name-<N>` properties on the `pmu,spmi` device-tree nodes). This is a hard limit, not a gap in the testing: there is **no native way to fake a thermal shutdown cause**. The value is produced by the PMU at power-off and exposed read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store — `sysctl -w` refuses (read-only OID), there is no user-settable IORegistry path, no `nvram` variable, and a userspace `os_log` line would not carry the right sender image. Generating real heat was out of scope. **The thermal path should not be described as verified in any customer-facing text or release note.** - **The real IOKit read on CI.** macOS VMs expose no PMU, so the property is absent and the reader returns empty. No E2E test is added; on a virtualized runner one could only assert graceful degradation, which is worth having but would not be thermal coverage. ### Additional Notes **Known tradeoff — `crash` fires on user force-restarts.** Measured, not hypothetical: `crash,crash0_in` appeared in pattern C with no panic induced. The token means the AP's CRASH line was asserted, which a hard reset satisfies, so **every user-initiated force restart on this hardware emits a `crash`-classified event.** Accepted because a force restart is itself a signal that something went wrong badly enough that the user gave up on the machine, and the alternative — treating the family as benign — silently dropped genuine AP and hypervisor crashes. Two commitments follow: the message says "followed a CRASH signal from the processor" and never claims a kernel panic; and if force restarts dominate emitted volume, the fix is to split `crash,hyp_*` from `crash,crash*_in`, not to revert the family to benign. **Fault allowlist, not benign denylist.** Under a denylist, any Mac whose clean shutdown emits an uncatalogued token would raise a shutdown-fault event on *every boot*. A permanent false positive is noticed and distrusted; a missed rare fault is not. The cost is that a genuinely new fault token on unfamiliar hardware is dropped silently — mitigated by matching on the family *prefix*, so `ot,anything_new` still classifies thermal. **Two benign per-token exceptions** (`shutdownBenignTokens`), for tokens whose family is a fault but whose meaning is not: `buck_boot_charge` (booting after the battery charged from depleted, not a regulator failure) and `timeout,dblclick_timeout` (the power-button double-click window). Both produced a user-visible fault event on a machine that had not faulted. Scoped to these two deliberately — the other `buck_*` tokens name real regulator failures. Excluding one only changes the outcome when it is the sole evidence for its class. **Graceful degradation is strictly additive** — nothing here can block `Start()` or interfere with crash-report collection. Property absent → no event, debug log. IOKit failure → no event. `kern.bootsessionuuid` unreadable → skip the whole check, since without a dedup key an event could repeat on every Agent restart. `kern.boottime` unreadable → fall back to the current time and omit `boot_time`. Event over the wire limit → drop and warn, **never truncate a fault payload**, because a truncated one would be misleading. Save-failure and saturation warnings latch so a persistent condition warns once rather than on every reconcile tick, and are kept separate so neither can silence the other. **Bounds are derived from real hardware, and shared between C and Go so they cannot drift.** `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SERVICE 88` and `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS 53` come from the largest known real payload (80-token dictionary, longest token 35 bytes) plus margin — 10% on count, 50% on length — and the Go-side `maxShutdownTokens` / `maxShutdownTokenBytes` are derived from those same macros. `DD_PMU_MAX_SERVICES` is 16, matching how few PMU-publishing services exist in practice. A service exceeding its bounds is dropped and logged rather than failing the read; an oversized token is truncated rather than dropping its whole service; the walk stops early once every distinct token is accounted for, since no remaining service can contribute one that has not been seen. **Intel Macs silently emit nothing.** `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not exist there; `readPMUBootFaultInfo` returns `errShutdownCauseUnsupported` when `runtime.GOARCH != "arm64"`. The Intel path (SMC shutdown-cause code `-81` via `log show`, which needs root) is unimplemented and unvalidated — no Intel Mac available. Apple documents none of this property: `org:apple-oss-distributions` returns zero hits for both `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` and `info-fault_name`. Provenance is the device's own ADT table, community string dumps of the `AppleD2255PMU` kext, and independent confirmation of the prefix decodings in `hack-different/apple-knowledge`. The *read mechanism*, by contrast, is entirely public API: `IOServiceMatching`, `IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorNext`, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.

signals.title: feat(otel-metrics): share SDK trace stats mapping
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a transport-neutral `sdktracestats` package under `opentelemetry-mapping-go`. `BuildSDKTraceStatsPayload` owns SDK metric recognition, field mapping, validation, normalized tags, time windows, per-datapoint error isolation, and lossless sparse-histogram construction. The caller supplies envelope metadata such as source and hostname. The package returns shared APM-stats fields without depending on the Agent or dd-source protobuf types. ### Motivation The Agent and public OTLP metrics intake need to convert `traces.span.sdk.metrics.duration` into the same APM trace-stats contract. Keeping two mappings would let tags, status handling, histogram validation, and operation naming drift. This PR makes one mapping implementation the source of truth while leaving transport adapters and delivery local to each consumer. ### Stack and shipping order 1. This PR merges first as the shared code dependency. 2. [ddoghq/dd-source#56526](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/56526) and [DataDog/datadog-agent#53167](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53167) then consume it and can be reviewed in parallel. 3. [ddoghq/dd-go#8800](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-go/pull/8800) can merge independently, but it must deploy before #53167 rolls out. The dd-source rollout does not depend on dd-go. ### Scope - Delta histograms only; the mapping keeps no cumulative-to-delta state. - Invalid datapoints are skipped without discarding valid datapoints in the same metric. - Exact explicit histogram data is preserved in sparse-sketch fields. - No protobuf, HTTP, routing, or deployment behavior is introduced here. ### Validation - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/opentelemetry-mapping-go/otlp/metrics/...` - `bazel test //pkg/opentelemetry-mapping-go/otlp/metrics/sdktracestats:sdktracestats_test` Both suites pass. Contract coverage includes field mapping, tag normalization, explicit histograms, invalid-datapoint isolation, temporality filtering, fallback windows, and large sparse-bin counts. ### Review focus - Shared field and tag semantics. - Validation/error-isolation behavior. - The boundary between shared mapping logic and consumer-owned transport code.

The file is mounted into the container and xcopied into the buildroot, so `get_version()` reads the cache and never calls `git describe`. ### Motivation Full clones of this repo are expensive. signals.title: feat(autodiscovery): report ignored keys when AD formats are mixed
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Autodiscovery applies one check configuration format per entity — v2 (`checks`), then v1 (`check_names` + `init_configs` + `instances`), then legacy — and until now the ones that lost were dropped silently. This reports them through the errors `extractTemplatesFromMapWithV2` already collects, so they surface in `agent status` under `Configuration Errors` and as an AD annotation health issue. That function is the common entry point for pod annotations, container labels and Kubernetes service/endpoints annotations. ``` ad.datadoghq.com/server.checks takes precedence, ignoring ad.datadoghq.com/server.check_names, ad.datadoghq.com/server.init_configs, ad.datadoghq.com/server.instances: Autodiscovery only applies the check configuration with the highest priority (v2, then v1, then legacy) ``` Detection is limited to the keys that define a check: `ignore_autodiscovery_tags` and `logs` are excluded because they are read next to a v2 configuration — the former is applied on top of one when `cluster_checks.support_hybrid_ignore_ad_tags` is enabled. Following #41372, this uses the stored errors rather than a log line. ### Motivation A team on a cluster we operate followed the docs and added a v2 annotation to a workload that already had v1 ones, and their existing checks silently stopped — no warning, no log line, nothing in `agent status`. Both forms are valid Autodiscovery syntax, so nothing looked wrong at a glance, and finding the cause took a while. The precedence is intentional, but it is documented only in a code comment. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added cases for v1 next to v2 and v1 next to legacy; six existing mixed-format cases were updated. The single-format cases still assert no error, and the hybrid-mode case in `kube_services_test.go` guards the exclusion above. ### Additional Notes Users who mix formats today will see a new error in `agent status` and a new AD annotation health issue (`MEDIUM`); the applied configuration does not change. Follow-ups not included: the health issue's remediation steps, documenting the precedence rule, and reporting a standalone `check_tag_cardinality` that is dropped next to a v2 configuration.

signals.title: fix(ebpf): synchronize perfUsageCollector.Collect with Manager.Start
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race between `perfUsageCollector.Collect` (reads PerfMap/RingBuffer telemetry fields during a Prometheus Gather tick) and `Manager.Start` (writes those fields during eBPF manager startup). Adds a shared `sync.Mutex` (`TelemetryMu`) in `pkg/ebpf` that both `Start` and `Collect` hold. It lives in `pkg/ebpf` to avoid a circular import (`pkg/ebpf/telemetry` already imports `pkg/ebpf`). ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — the race requires eBPF support to trigger (`Manager.Start` writes to PerfMap/RingBuffer internal fields that can't be constructed in a unit test). The race is eliminated by construction: `Collect` and `Start` now share the same mutex, so they can never access the telemetry fields concurrently.

Sets `logs_config.stop_grace_period` to 0 and wraps `agent.stop()` in `sync.OnceFunc` in the logs agent test suites, reducing `TestRestartTestSuite` from 70s to 33s and `TestAgentTestSuite` from 41s to 17s. ### Motivation The cleanup registered by `createAgent` and the explicit `agent.stop()` calls in test methods both invoked `stopComponents`, which blocked for 5s each on non-idempotent component `Stop()` methods (e.g. `fileLauncher.Stop()` blocks on an unbuffered channel when `Start()` was never called); the 5s grace period added another 5s per call. ### Describe how you validated your changes Both test suites were run in full before and after the change to confirm all tests still pass and measure the speedup. ### Additional Notes All changes are test-only; no non-test code was modified.

signals.title: Report DDOT process state in the installer agent state
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `ddot_process_state` line to the agent state the fleet installer daemon reports through the remote-config client. It is set on the `datadog-agent` package entry, next to the existing stable/experiment version and config version. The state is read from `dd-procmgrd` over its socket (gRPC on a UDS on Linux, a named pipe on Windows — the `dd-procmgr` binary is never invoked) when the process manager supervises DDOT, and falls back to systemd on Linux / the service manager on Windows otherwise. This reuses `pkg/procmgr/coat`, which already performs exactly that collection for COAT telemetry and already carries a `ddot` entry in its service catalog; the new `Snapshot.ServiceProcessState` only maps a collected snapshot onto a reported value. Reported values: `running`, `starting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `created`, `crashed`, `exited`, `failed` when procmgr supervises DDOT; `running` when the legacy systemd unit or Windows service is active; `not_installed` when DDOT is absent; `unknown` when procmgr owns it but is unreachable; and `""` only when nothing can be determined, so the backend can tell "not reported" from "no DDOT on this host". The probe is bounded (2s) and cannot fail a state refresh — it returns a string only, never an error. ### Motivation The update monitoring uses the reported agent state to decide whether an update succeeded. Now that DDOT can be updated on its own (version or config), the state had no way to express whether the DDOT process actually came back up afterwards. This matters because a broken DDOT does not end an experiment by itself: the core agent does not read `otel-config.yaml`, so the experiment agent stays healthy, and `dd-procmgrd` retries a failing child forever rather than giving up. The reported process state is therefore the only signal that can tell the backend not to promote. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests: - `pkg/procmgr/coat/process_state_test.go` — every `pb.ProcessState`, both legacy supervisor modes, not-installed, procmgr-unreachable, installed-without-supervisor, unknown service ID. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/ddot_state_test.go` — the collector seam (nil collector, procmgr running/failed, systemd, not-installed) and a `refreshState` test asserting the field lands only on the `datadog-agent` entry. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/local_api_test.go` — the field round-trips through the local API `/status`. Ran: `bazel test //pkg/procmgr/coat:coat_test //pkg/fleet/daemon:daemon_test`, `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/proto/pbgo/core` (msgp round-trip), `bazel build //cmd/installer/...`, `dda inv linter.go`. Generated protobuf code is committed and `dda inv protobuf.generate` is a no-op on the tree. E2E — new `TestDDOTConfigFailureReportsFailedAndReverts` in the fleet config suite (Linux, runs in the existing `new-e2e-fleet-config` job with no CI wiring changes): 1. Install the agent and the `ddot` extension; assert DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd`, launched with the stable `otel-config.yaml`, reported as `running`. 2. Start a config experiment patching `/otel-config.yaml` with an invalid debug-exporter verbosity; assert the broken config reaches the experiment collector and DDOT is unhealthy. 3. Assert the reported `ddot_process_state` becomes `failed`. 4. Assert nothing promoted it: `experiment_config_version` still set, `stable_config_version` unchanged, stable config free of the bad value. 5. Mimic the backend reacting to that state by sending the revert task (`stop_experiment_config`). 6. Assert the revert landed: `experiment_config_version` cleared, `stable_config_version` never changed, stable `otel-config.yaml` restored byte-for-byte, DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd` on the stable config, reported state back to `running`. ### Additional Notes - **The failure state is `failed`, not `crashed`.** `CRASHED` exists in the proto and Go enums but the Rust process manager never emits it: `set_last_status` maps any non-zero exit or signal to `Failed`. - **`restart: on-failure` never gives up on DDOT.** With `restart_sec: 2`, backoff ×2 capped at 60s, and `start_limit_burst: 5` over a 10s window, attempts land at t≈0, 2, 6, 14, 30, 62… — never 5 within any 10s window, so DDOT loops `Failed → Starting → Failed` indefinitely and `dd-procmgrd` stays up. - Field 17 is new, so older backends skip it and newer backends see `""` from older agents. The msgp decoder skips unknown fields, so mixed-version marshalling is safe. - During a version experiment, `Installed`/`ProcmgrConfigured` are resolved from the daemon's own install root while the process state comes from the shared procmgr socket. That only affects the `unknown`-vs-`stopped` distinction; the running state stays correct, since the stable and experiment procmgr share one socket and the DDOT process definition filename is invariant (only `${DD_CONF_DIR}` differs).

signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [ABLD-294] Bump `rules_go` to embed `go.mod` data in Go binaries
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Bump `rules_go` from 0.61.1 to 0.63.0 in `MODULE.bazel`, and the matching Go module in `go.mod` for the runfiles and test helpers. Declare `_cgo_godefs` with `go_rule`, and regenerate the `vtproto` files, both of which 0.63.0 requires. ### Motivation [ABLD-294](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/ABLD-294). bazel-contrib/rules_go#4595 threads Gazelle-generated package metadata into the link action, so `runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo().Deps` now reports module versions the way `go build` does, which is what security scanners read. bazel-contrib/rules_go#4690 completes the pair by passing the main package import path, the field those clients read to tell which binary they are looking at. 0.63.0 is the first release carrying either, and pulling them from the BCR avoids keeping that work as a local patch. ### Describe how you validated your changes Concrete example: ``` bazel build //cmd/config-stream-client bazel run //:go -- version -m "$(bazel cquery //cmd/config-stream-client --output=files)" ``` - before: ``` bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/cmd/config-stream-client/config-stream-client_/config-stream-client: go1.26.5 ``` - after: ``` bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/cmd/config-stream-client/config-stream-client_/config-stream-client: go1.26.5 path github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/cmd/config-stream-client dep cloud.google.com/go/auth v0.20.0 dep cloud.google.com/go/auth/oauth2adapt v0.2.8 dep cloud.google.com/go/compute v1.64.0 dep cloud.google.com/go/compute/metadata v0.9.0 dep github.com/DataDog/agent-payload/v5 v5.0.209 dep github.com/beorn7/perks v1.0.1 dep github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2 v2.3.0 dep github.com/davecgh/go-spew v1.1.2-0.20180830191138-d8f796af33cc dep github.com/felixge/httpsnoop v1.0.4 dep github.com/go-logr/logr v1.4.3 dep github.com/go-logr/stdr v1.2.2 dep github.com/go-viper/mapstructure/v2 v2.5.0 dep github.com/gofrs/flock v0.13.0 dep github.com/google/s2a-go v0.1.9 dep github.com/googleapis/enterprise-certificate-proxy v0.3.15 dep github.com/googleapis/gax-go/v2 v2.22.0 dep github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/v2 v2.3.3 dep github.com/mdlayher/socket v0.6.0 dep github.com/mdlayher/vsock v1.3.0 dep github.com/mohae/deepcopy v0.0.0-20170929034955-c48cc78d4826 dep github.com/munnerz/goautoneg v0.0.0-20191010083416-a7dc8b61c822 dep github.com/philhofer/fwd v1.2.0 dep github.com/pmezard/go-difflib v1.0.1-0.20181226105442-5d4384ee4fb2 dep github.com/prometheus/client_golang v1.24.1 dep github.com/prometheus/client_model v0.6.2 dep github.com/prometheus/common v0.70.1 dep github.com/prometheus/procfs v0.21.1 dep github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4 v4.26.7 dep github.com/spf13/cast v1.8.0 dep github.com/stretchr/testify v1.11.1 dep github.com/tinylib/msgp v1.6.4 dep github.com/tklauser/go-sysconf v0.3.16 dep github.com/tklauser/numcpus v0.11.0 dep go.opentelemetry.io/auto/sdk v1.2.1 dep go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp v0.69.0 dep go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.44.1-0.20260622141720-fbe3d073ba93 dep go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric v1.44.1-0.20260622141720-fbe3d073ba93 dep go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace v1.44.1-0.20260622141720-fbe3d073ba93 dep go.uber.org/atomic v1.11.0 dep go.uber.org/dig v1.19.0 dep go.uber.org/fx v1.24.0 dep go.uber.org/multierr v1.11.0 dep go.uber.org/zap v1.28.0 dep go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 v2.4.4 dep go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5 dep golang.org/x/crypto v0.54.0 dep golang.org/x/net v0.57.0 dep golang.org/x/oauth2 v0.36.0 dep golang.org/x/sync v0.22.0 dep golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 dep golang.org/x/text v0.40.0 dep golang.org/x/time v0.15.0 dep google.golang.org/api v0.279.0 dep google.golang.org/genproto v0.0.0-20260319201613-d00831a3d3e7 dep google.golang.org/genproto/googleapis/api v0.0.0-20260615183401-62b3387ff324 dep google.golang.org/genproto/googleapis/rpc v0.0.0-20260618152121-87f3d3e198d3 dep google.golang.org/grpc v1.83.0 dep google.golang.org/protobuf v1.36.12-0.20260116114154-8c4c4ae446ca dep gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 ``` `bazel test //pkg/ebpf:verify_generated_files` passes with and without `--config=gorace`, entirely from cache, so `cgo_godefs` keeps emitting the same files now that it declares a C/C++ toolchain. `bazel mod explain rules_go` resolves every consumer to 0.63.0, and `package_metadata`, newly required by `rules_go`, to the 0.0.13 already in the graph. ### Additional Notes `Path` and `Deps` are populated, whereas main module identity and build settings such as `vcs.revision` stay empty, which upstream will address later. Upstream skips the `c-archive`, `c-shared` and `plugin` link modes, which nothing in the tree uses. An empty main module identity is still observable: `vtproto` stamps a version comment whenever `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` reports anything, so its six generated files gain a `protoc-gen-go-vtproto version:` line carrying no value until upstream reports that field. bazel-contrib/rules_go#4601 dropped the fallback letting a rule reach a cgo-capable `go_context()` without declaring a C/C++ toolchain, which `--config=gorace` turns into a `cgo is disabled` analysis failure, hence the `go_rule` declaration. A module is listed only if Gazelle wrote it a `pkg:golang` label, and Gazelle writes that label **only when it also generates the module's build files**, which the `build_file_generation = "auto"` set in `deps/go.MODULE.bazel` skips for a module shipping its own. That silently omits 9 third-party modules, of which `//cmd/...` links `grpc-gateway/v2`, `resty/v2`, `cel.dev/expr` and `protoc-gen-validate`. The 27 in-tree submodules it also omits are first-party and remapped to in-tree labels anyway. Two other fixes in this range are worth naming: - bazel-contrib/rules_go#4649 restores the param file 0.61 dropped, which produced `Argument list too long` on large command lines, - bazel-contrib/rules_go#4671 passes `-ffile-prefix-map` so `__FILE__` in cgo stops embedding absolute paths. Nothing becomes removable, since bazel-contrib/rules_go#3977 is still open and no other in-tree workaround references `rules_go`. Prospective next steps: - report main module identity and build settings, the part of ABLD-294 this bump leaves out, which needs upstream work, and which also fills in the `vtproto` version comments, - label the 9 modules Gazelle leaves unlabeled, either through `build_file_generation` `on` or by decoupling label from generation, - measure path mapping, maintained again through bazel-contrib/rules_go#4663 and bazel-contrib/rules_go#4667, since stripping configuration directories lets the transitioned binary configurations share remote cache entries. [ABLD-294]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/ABLD-294?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: Enables the v3 metrics intake for series in DDOT
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Enables the **v3 metrics intake for series** in DDOT (the `otel-agent` binary). By default is ON with extra requirements: - no proxy - only recognized Datadog sites ### Motivation OTAGENT-1130, under epic OTAGENT-1133 ("Reduce customer metrics egress bandwidth 30–50% with v3 payload"). DDOT was the last OTel surface still on the v2 series intake. This PR moves DDOT onto the v3 series path, aligning it with the core Agent (series v3 default since 7.81). ### Describe how you validated your changes - **Unit:** `cmd/otel-agent/config` tests pass; the guard tests now assert the resolved value is `datadog_only`. - **Static:** `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues; `dda inv otel-agent.build` — OK. - **Manual (local, standalone otel-agent → fakeintake, `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=true`, zstd):** series routed to `/api/intake/metrics/v3/series` and **0** on `/api/v2/series`; all payloads zstd (wire magic `28b52ffd`); v3 payloads decode correctly; a cumulative Sum arrived as a delta `COUNT` (c2d); sketches stayed on `/api/beta/sketches` (v2). - **Manual + telemetrygen + delta** - metrics are posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **Manual + telemetrygen + cumulative** - metrics are converted to delta & posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **E2E:** new `TestOTelAgentV3Series` (KinD DDOT with v3 enabled) asserts OTLP metrics reach the intake, series land on the v3 endpoint (`RouteStats`), and v3 payloads are zstd. Auto-wired into the `new-e2e-otel` job — no CI changes. (Runs in CI on this PR.) ### Additional Notes - **Kill-switch / rollout:** enablement follows `use_v3_api.series.enabled` (default `datadog_only`). v2 remains the compat/fallback path (non-Datadog destinations, non-zstd builds, non-migrated regions). Opt out with `use_v3_api.series.enabled=false` (or `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=false`). - **Scope:** series only. Sketches (distributions) stay on v2 (v3 for sketches is a separate opt-in). - **Known follow-up (this PR):** the auto-injected `datadog/dd-autoconfigured` flare extension keeps its own zlib serializer and now logs a benign but misleading "disabling v3 metrics intake" warning — the same warning #52301 suppressed on the OSS path, surfaced because v3 is now enabled in-process. Egress is unaffected (verified v3 + zstd); the warning does not reflect the actual series path. To be addressed. - this deliberately does **not** revert #52301 (`serializerexporter/serializer.go`). That line only runs for the OSS Datadog exporter in opentelemetry-collector-contrib - for case "datadog_only" - the PR updates "use_v3_api.series.endpoints" by "https://api.xxxx" https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1130

signals.title: feat(vdi): add Amazon DCV core metrics
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? - Registers an opt-in Windows VDI core check for Amazon WorkSpaces. - Collects Amazon DCV performance counters through PDH. - Emits DCV metrics, platform tags, and the `vdi.dcv.health` service check. - Treats version-specific optional counters as debug-level omissions. ### Motivation This is the first functional slice of VDI monitoring. It provides useful Amazon DCV performance metrics without depending on privileged session inventory or system-probe, so it can be reviewed and validated independently before adding enrichment. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/vdi,./pkg/util/pdhutil` - `env GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/vdi,./pkg/util/pdhutil` The focused core-check test passed after rebasing onto the latest `main`. `pkg/util/pdhutil` is Windows-only and therefore has no test package on the local macOS host; it was covered by the Windows-targeted lint/compile gate. Manually validated the successful Windows path on an Amazon WorkSpaces Personal host using the non-FIPS Windows artifact from pipeline `131649377` / job `1961998574`: - Installed the artifact built from commit `efc81c6b` and confirmed the Agent reported that commit. - Confirmed the package ships only `conf.yaml.example`; the VDI check was not enabled automatically. - Enabled a minimal `aws_workspaces` / `personal` instance and ran `agent check vdi` successfully. - Collected 151 samples per run across server, session, connection, channel, imaging, and process metrics. - Confirmed `vdi.dcv.health` reported OK. - Confirmed representative monotonic counters such as `vdi.dcv.server.total_sessions` and `vdi.dcv.server.received_bytes` were emitted as counts in rate mode. - Confirmed the expected `vdi_provider:aws_workspaces`, `vdi_protocol:dcv`, and `workspaces_product:personal` tags were present. - Confirmed an instance-level custom QA tag appeared exactly once on metrics and the service check. - Confirmed the long-running Agent scheduled the check successfully with 151 samples and one service check per run, without VDI warnings or errors. ### Additional Notes This PR is the first draft in a three-PR stack. The PRs will be reviewed and validated in order: 1. **[#55009 — Amazon DCV core metrics](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55009)** (this PR) 2. [#55010 — Privileged session enrichment through system-probe](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55010) 3. signals.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signals.title: fix(ssi): run host SSI instrument-start/stop before Docker run
signals.text: In a stale state (ld.preload pointing to a non existent tmp injector), Docker doesn't start correctly. We should always run the SSI installer before Docker to clean/repair ld.preload file. Also always run the shutdown phase, even if the start was not successful (stop is idempotent).

signals.title: [AAD-6] Unify detector point windows
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > 1. This is mostly for metrics that arrive every 15s, I'm thinking about how to properly manage logs that are every 1s in a future PR (instead of a 30m retention they have 2m retention this way) -> [comment](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024#discussion_r3802840340). > 2. The end goal is to unify storage when we do the warmup, some values are duplicated (future PR). This unifies all detectors (except RRCF) with an interface to get the min / max number of points per series. This way there is no discrepancy with the storage max retention (now deduced by default [1]). Warmup lazy behavior: Max retention behavior [2]: Detectors follow these conditions: 1. A new series has < min points -> no detector state created (discarded) 2. A new series has min points -> create initial state 3. The series has > min and < max points -> process + can trigger anomalies 4. The series has < min points now but had before > min points -> process (update state only if needed) but don't trigger anomalies 5. Internal detector states have max MaxPoints state points (we don't have a state for a point not present in the storage) 6. A new series can't have > max points nor > max state points (eviction) It improves memory / CPU since series that have few points don't have state, it's lazy computation. signals.title: [NETPATH-1118] Add baseline dynamic tests for CNM
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds opt-in baseline Dynamic Tests for Cloud Network Monitoring. Baseline mode observes eligible CNM traffic over a bounded window, selects up to five representative high-volume paths per Agent, and runs each winner once. #### Product contract - Baseline is a best-effort, automatically curated preview of Network Path. It does not guarantee coverage for a particular connection or destination. - The budget is per Agent: each completed window produces at most five baseline test runs. - Baseline favors stable, important traffic in v1. Diversity, rotation, and diagnostic-signal prioritization are intentionally deferred. - Standard connection-monitoring Dynamic Tests take precedence when enabled. #### Window lifecycle - The first window after baseline starts is five minutes to reduce time to first value. - Later windows are one hour. This cadence is intentionally separate from `network_path.collector.pathtest_interval`, which continues to control recurring Network Path tests. - Candidate ranking is updated continuously as CNM snapshots arrive. Admission is intentionally streaming: a periodic flush may split a concurrently processed snapshot across adjacent windows. This is a known and accepted limitation. - At each boundary, the final winners are submitted once and selection state is reset for the next window. #### Selection - Eligibility and filtering remain upstream. Baseline consumes already-admitted paths without depending on whether built-in, local, or Remote Configuration filtering admitted them. - Observations use the collector's existing normalized path identity: origin, namespace, hostname or IP, effective port, protocol, and source container ID. - A path's score is cumulative sent plus received bytes observed during the window. - Selection uses a weighted Space-Saving heavy-hitter estimator with a fixed 32-candidate set, keeping memory bounded independently of connection count. - Stable path identity provides deterministic tie-breaking. #### Execution - Winners are one-shot baseline executions rather than recurring TTL-backed contexts. - Existing queues, workers, concurrency controls, and rate limits remain shared with other Network Path tests. - A queue drop, rate-limit rejection, or execution failure does not restore the slot, promote another candidate, or trigger catch-up work. - Successful results carry `dynamic_test_profile: "baseline"`. ### Motivation Selecting paths independently from each CNM snapshot can accumulate recurring contexts and produce unstable coverage. Windowed heavy-hitter selection gives baseline a predictable contract: observe traffic over a meaningful period, choose up to five stable high-volume paths, and run each once. ### Test coverage requirements Comprehensive coverage is an acceptance requirement for this change. Tests must cover: - cumulative sent-plus-received byte ranking across multiple snapshots and repeated paths; - the five-minute bootstrap window, subsequent hourly windows, streaming boundary rollover, the accepted adjacent-window snapshot split, reset behavior, partial sets, and empty windows; - bounded candidate memory, heavy-hitter retention, deterministic ties, and overflow-safe accumulation; - the fixed baseline cadence, independence from `pathtest_interval`, and Standard Dynamic Tests precedence; - at-most-five one-shot submissions, including no replacement or retry after input-queue pressure or rate limiting; - preservation of filtering/Remote Configuration provenance and baseline payload attribution; - byte propagation from both CNM connection producers; - race safety for selector and store lifecycle changes; - a packaged-Agent E2E path through CNM traffic, system-probe traceroute, payload encoding, and fakeintake delivery. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/rdnsquerier/impl:impl_test //pkg/config/setup:setup_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel test --config=gorace //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test` - `bazel coverage //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test --combined_report=lcov` (100% line coverage for `baseline.go`; 97.5% for `pathteststore.go`) - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test` The live AWS E2E has not yet been run. A passing packaged-Agent E2E is required before merge; its test binary compiles and CI wiring runs the netpath E2E job for the affected implementation paths. Local `dda inv` lint/test commands could not start because the internal Go toolchain mirror was not resolvable. Bazel validation above completed successfully. ### Additional Notes - Baseline uses a fixed five-test hourly budget, separate from `pathtest_interval`, so preview volume stays predictable without changing standard or NetFlow cadence. - The two connection-adapter paths are included in the netpath E2E change rules so byte-propagation changes continue to exercise this coverage. - This PR targets `main` directly and is not stacked on #54938.

signals.title: fix(e2e): flush fakeintake between flare suite tests (FLREM-153)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `BeforeTest` override to `baseFlareSuite` (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/flare_common_test.go`) that flushes the fakeintake before each test, following the "one fakeintake per suite" convention documented in `test/new-e2e/AGENTS.md`. ### Motivation In e2e tests each test suite has its own fakeintake. Any test within a test suite uses the same fakeintake instance. `BeforeTest` fakeintake flush ensures that a test starts with an empty fakeintake, with no flares. `TestFlareDefaultFiles` has been flaking with `"Could not find diagnose.log file in flare archive"` (tracked in [FLREM-153](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153)). The suite never reset the fakeintake between tests, so `GetLatestFlare()` — which just returns `payloads[len(payloads)-1]` — could pick up a flare left over from a previous test, or from the framework's post-failure diagnose-flare upload, instead of the one just requested by the current test. FLREM-153 also covers a second, unrelated flake (`TestLocalFlareDefaultFiles` hitting `context deadline exceeded` on the flare POST, due to the agent's hardcoded 60s HTTP client timeout combined with infra slowness). That one isn't addressed here — see the ticket comment for details. ### Describe how you validated your changes Traced the mechanics through `test/e2e-framework/testing/e2e/suite.go` (`BaseSuite.BeforeTest`/`AfterTest`/`IsDevMode`), `test/e2e-framework/testing/environments/host.go` (post-failure diagnose flare upload), and `test/fakeintake/client/client.go` (`FlushServerAndResetAggregators`, `GetLatestFlare`) to confirm the fix addresses the root cause and matches the identical pattern already used by ~10-15 other suites in this tree. ### Additional Notes [FLREM-153]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: Also stop the coverage job from thrashing Bazel analysis cache
signals.text: ### Motivation "Bazel analysis cache thrashing on `main` (containerized job)" keeps alerting after #54963 ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1963914110)): all 49 occurrences of the last 24 hours come from `bazel:coverage:linux-amd64`, which now flips `cover_format`, `--collect_code_coverage` and `--instrumentation_filter`. The last one `bazel coverage` derives from the target patterns, some 400 package regexes that a post-test command cannot replay. ### What does this PR do? Skip `test2json` and UTOF where their `bazel run` cannot match the test invocation, which is only the coverage job: its tests are a **subset** of `bazel:test:linux-amd64`, still reporting them, while its JUnit tar needs no Bazel and its coverage profile only `bazel info`, which analyzes nothing. Guard the remaining `bazel run` with `--noallow_analysis_cache_discard`, turning a future divergence into a failure of the job that introduces it, rather than a warning nobody reads until a monitor fires hours later on `main` pipelines. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv bazel.process-test-results --result-json=` runs no Bazel and still packages JUnit, while a non-empty one keeps converting logs. With the server left in the coverage configuration, the guarded command exits 2 on "analysis cache would have been discarded", and stays silent after `bazel test --config=gorace`. ### Additional Notes The guard is safe for the four `bazel:test:*` jobs: `INSTALL_DIR` and `AGENT_FLAVOR` are set by packaging jobs only, so `omnibazel_flags` injects nothing there, and neither monitor has reported a flip in those jobs since #54963.

signals.title: Convert linux_bpf to linux && bpf build tags
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Bazel requires a hint to understand whether a certain package is OS specific or not. One of the ways to do that is to use platform build tags like `linux`, `windows`, etc. In our case `linux_bpf` was de facto a platform constraint, but Bazel and Gazelle, a tool we use to automatically manage BUILD files, were not aware of that, so certain Linux only libraries were becoming unconditional dependencies for all the platforms. That was leading to failed builds and test executions. So, the simplest way out of this was to rename `linux_bpf` into `bpf` and add `linux` tag everywhere to have `linux && bpf`. ### Motivation First, it is technically more correct to rely more on standard go build tags. Second, this paves us the way to get rid of `bpf` tag in the near future. ### Additional Notes **Go Package Import Differences** is a false positive. Change in build tags led to a change in baseline being pretty much empty for the new layout. There are no changes in the imports

signals.title: Convert Bazel test logs to test2json in-graph via aspect
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Converts each Bazel `test.log` to test2json **during** `bazel test`, via an aspect on `TestRunner` actions, instead of shelling out to a converter afterwards. `tasks/bazel.py` then concatenates the resulting fragments. It already parsed the BEP to collect `test.xml` for JUnit, so fragment locations are picked up in that same pass, and `process-test-results` no longer invokes Bazel at all. Enabled by `--config=test2json`. Bazel's `coverage` command inherits `test` options, so the `test:` lines cover both. ### Motivation The previous flow ran `bazel run //bazel/tools/testlogs_to_json` in `after_script` over a hand-maintained label/log manifest, carrying `--config=gorace` purely to keep its analysis cache aligned with the test invocation's. Conversion is naturally per-test work, so it belongs in the graph where it is cached and parallelised alongside the tests. It also means the logs no longer have to come to us: since conversion happens where the log is produced, CI no longer force-downloads every `test.log` (`--remote_download_regex` dropped). ### Describe how you validated your changes Local runs on macOS arm64, against the previous manifest-based converter as the baseline: output is semantically identical on the same BEP; failing targets still publish their fragments and tests execute exactly once; after `bazel clean` with 9 of 10 tests served from remote cache, all 10 fragments materialised under `--remote_download_outputs=toplevel`; `--runs_per_test=2` yields uniquely named fragments per run; `bazel coverage` publishes the group; a BEP from a run without the aspect gives an actionable error. Unit tests cover the converter, the BEP fragment resolution and the merge; `buildifier`, `gofmt` and `ruff` clean. CI exercises the five reporting jobs on real `//...` invocations. ### Additional Notes **The Bazel label, not the Go import path, is the test2json package.** `dd_agent_go_test` emits several configured `go_test` targets for one Go package under different build-tag sets; collapsing them to one import path makes UTOF report distinct runs as retries of each other. **Trade-off:** conversion moves onto the critical path of the test invocation, adding one small action per test target. In exchange those actions are cached and shared, so re-runs with cache hits do no conversion work. **Cached tests are restamped.** test2json records `Time` when a log is converted, and the conversion is cached alongside the test it describes, so a cached test would otherwise replay timestamps from whenever its fragment was first built — UTOF, which derives duration from the first-to-last event span, reported a day-old cache hit as 20h of run time. The merge rewrites `Time` on fragments the BEP marks as cache hits. Consequence: a fully-cached run reports no overall duration rather than a wrong one. **Rules with `analysis_test = True`** (skylib `analysistest` and friends) may not register actions, and the restriction covers aspects applied to them, so they produce no fragment — 23 of 1451 test targets in `//...`. They were already excluded from the JUnit tar, and their conversion only ever produced a package-level pass/fail with no test functions. A failing analysis test still fails the job; it is only absent from the test2json artifact.

signals.title: feat(ssi): last-TRUE-wins SSI matching
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Unify SSI matching on a single last-TRUE-wins matcher: - **Static targets** (Helm / Operator / `datadog.yaml`) are reversed at construction so config first-wins is preserved. - **RC policies** keep wire order (catch-all first, exceptions after) and are last-TRUE-wins as-is. - Evaluation is static first, then RC, then SSI inject-all only when both are absent. A matched deny does not fall through. ``` SSI | static targets | RC | Decision off | — | none | nothing off | — | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | none | none | everything on | none | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | present | none | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else nothing on | present | policies | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else last matching policy, else nothing ``` Stacked on #55057. ### Motivation RC is already last-wins on the wire. Using the same matcher for static targets (by reversing them) avoids two matching modes. Static targeting is evaluated before RC so a remote deny cannot override an explicit local target. ### Describe how you validated your changes - [x] Unit tests: `./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/autoinstrumentation` - [ ] E2E `TestSSISuite/TestRemoteConfig` (HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny, LastMatchingRemotePolicyWins) ### Additional Notes `HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny` now expects the helm python workload to **keep** SSI when an RC deny matches `targeted-namespace`. signals.title: ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signals.text: #incident-59451 ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors, by giving apt real per-request failover: - Rewrites the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list (`us-west-2`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `mirror.leaseweb.net`) so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - Drops `us-east-1` (the chronically-slow mirror in the timeout logs). - `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error that triggers failover. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs, across many branches). The build spent its whole wall-clock in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror. A first attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** fix it: apt's `mirror` method sticks to one mirror per invocation and only fails over when it's fully unreachable, so a slow-but-reachable `us-east-1` kept timing out and `Acquire::Retries` retried the same URI to the job timeout. This PR switches to explicit ordered `URIs:` for genuine per-request failover. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs isolated mirror throughput as the only variable (successful same-commit runs finished in 16-21m). - Validated the `sed` `URIs:` rewrite against the default noble `ubuntu.sources`. - CI will exercise the real build here. ### Additional Notes The same fix is applied to the other CI Dockerfiles in #55119. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
signals.author: chouetz

signals.title: [7.82.x] ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signals.text: Backport of #55108 to `7.82.x`. ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors: - Adds `Acquire::Retries` + a 15s `Acquire` timeout so a stalled request is dropped and retried against the next mirror. - Lists mirrors as peers (drops the `priority:1` pin) and adds `us-west-2` and `mirror.leaseweb.net`, so apt load-balances and fails over across them. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs). The full 30-40m was spent in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror; the old `priority:1` pin only failed over when that mirror was fully unreachable, not when merely slow. ### Describe how you validated your changes Clean cherry-pick of the `main` commit. signals.title: fix(installer): secure Windows config rollback
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes Windows Fleet Automation config experiment rollback so it: - copies YAML ACLs from a securely created backup directory - removes only allowlisted Fleet-managed YAML that is absent from the backup - preserves unmanaged files and directories under `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` - rejects incomplete YAML copies and legacy symlink mismatches before deleting the backup - uses slash-aware allowlist matching and root-confined deletion to avoid over-deleting YAML or following swapped junctions - reconciles legacy v2 managed symlinks (`stable` / `experiment`) before robocopy and verifies they are restored Adds selective-cleanup, copy-validation, legacy-link, and Windows ACL/unmanaged-file regression tests, plus a release note. ### Motivation Addresses [WINA-2053](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053) and the failure observed in [SPFA-180](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180). The current `robocopy /MIR /SL ... *.yaml` rollback can purge destination content and recreates deleted files without their original ACLs. Adding `/SEC` by itself was previously unsafe because an unprivileged user could pre-create the destination between deletion and ACL repair while retaining an open handle. The current implementation now securely creates the experiment root with the stable root's security descriptor before copying, and never removes the stable root before restore. This change uses that prerequisite, removes `/MIR`, scopes rollback deletion in Go to managed YAML only, and treats robocopy mismatch exit codes 4-7 as rollback failure. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --no-cache` (64 passed) - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --only-modified-packages` - `bazelisk test //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config_test` - `bazelisk build //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config --platforms=@rules_go//go/toolchain:windows_amd64` - Pre-commit and pre-push hooks, including release-note validation Windows-only tests cover ACL restore, junction rejection, and v2 symlink rollback, including backups whose copied absolute `stable`/`experiment` links still point at the original tree (`robocopy /SL`). Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) [WINA-2053]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [SPFA-180]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: ci: make apt mirror config resilient to slow mirrors across agent images
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes CI Docker builds resilient to slow public package mirrors, across every image in this repo that installs packages from a public host — each fitted to its own package system. **Ubuntu (apt)** (`agent`, `base-image`, `cluster-agent`, `otel-agent`, `ddot-ebpf`, podman e2e resource): apt's `mirror` method can't fail over off a *slow* mirror (only a fully-unreachable one). The base image version is configurable (`BASE_IMAGE_UBUNTU_VERSION`), so we handle **both** apt source formats: - **deb822 `ubuntu.sources` (≥ 24.04):** rewrite the `URIs:` fields to an ordered multi-URI list so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - **legacy one-line `/etc/apt/sources.list` (< 24.04):** the format can't list multiple URIs per entry, so use `mirror+file` with a peer mirrorlist (fallback on an unreachable mirror). In both paths `us-east-1` is dropped (chronically slow in every timeout log), ordering `us-west-2` → `archive.ubuntu.com` → `mirror.leaseweb.net`, and `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout turns a slow mirror into a fast error. **Debian (apt)** (`test/fakeintake`, golang base): rewrite `debian.sources` `URIs:` to Debian's AWS/CloudFront mirror `cdn-aws.deb.debian.org` first, `deb.debian.org` fallback, + Acquire timeout/Retries. (Debian has no EC2 archive mirror like Ubuntu.) **Alpine (apk)** (`Dockerfiles/dogstatsd/alpine`, `test/fakeintake` deploy stage): list `dl-cdn` primary + `mirror.clarkson.edu` secondary (apk fails over in listed order), and add the global `apk --timeout` so a slow mirror fails fast. ### Motivation `docker_build_host_profiler_standalone_amd64` was timing out (~30m, across many branches). Its `release` stage builds on `agent-base-image` (= `Dockerfiles/agent/Dockerfile`), whose `apt-get` stalled against a congested `us-east-1`. An earlier attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** stop it: job `1965243524` showed apt sticking to the slow `us-east-1` and retrying the same URI to the job timeout, even though `us-west-2` served ~90 packages in one second when apt picked it. The `mirror` method has no per-request failover on slowness — hence the deb822 multi-URI switch. Review feedback on the first pass flagged that a deb822-only rewrite regressed pre-24.04 builds (the version is configurable, and one otel build uses 20.04, which has no `ubuntu.sources`). This PR therefore handles the legacy `sources.list` too, so no build silently loses mirror coverage. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs pinpointed the stall inside the apt step of the agent-base-image release stage on a slow `us-east-1`, and showed `us-west-2` healthy. - Validated the Ubuntu and Debian `sed` rewrites against the default noble `ubuntu.sources` / focal `sources.list` / trixie `debian.sources` (GNU sed semantics), and `bash -n` on the RUN body. - Confirmed `apk --timeout` is a valid global flag (must precede the subcommand). - CI will exercise the real builds here. ### Additional Notes Local dev-tooling Dockerfiles (`tools/gdb`, `tools/ebpf/*-agent-dev`) are excluded — they don't run under `CI=true` and aren't in any CI build path. `agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` was fixed separately in the already-merged quick-fix PR (#55108). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
