signal.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signal.text: Backport f776f333c334087d4b4c2f66b7f5dbaf4c051df6 from #55014. ___ ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signal.title: [procmgr] Config gates for processes.d auto-start
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds **config gates** to dd-procmgr so `processes.d` definitions can use `condition_config_any` to auto-start only when Agent config says they should. Implementation mirrors the Windows legacy SCM startup checks in `dependent_services_windows.go` and Agent config resolution: - YAML lookup (case-insensitive keys, flattened dotted keys, permissive parse fallback, merge keys) - Environment bindings (`DD_*`) with Agent precedence (ignore empty values, no trim before `ParseBool`, legacy `process_config.enabled` transforms) - Fleet policy merge - Derived `system_probe_config.enabled` (USM/NPM/security knobs, sk-tracer and discovery adjustments) - Windows: read `DD_*` overrides from the core Agent SCM `Environment` registry when not set in the procmgr process env Wires gate evaluation into `ManagedProcess` start/reload paths in the manager. **Stack context:** PR 2. Builds on [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) (`jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles`). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | This PR | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation Moving subservices (starting with process-agent) to dd-procmgr requires the supervisor to apply the same start/stop rules as the Agent today. Without config gates, a `processes.d` entry would always spawn when registered, which breaks parity with legacy SCM and fleet policy. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/` (env bindings, YAML load, system-probe derivations, gate evaluation) - Go unit tests for Windows config helpers (`pkg/config/setup/config_windows_test.go`) - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI ### Additional Notes - No `ENC[...]` / secret backend resolution in this PR (fleet policy `ENC[...]` values are not resolved here either). - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Schema comment sync in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/process_config.yaml` for env binding documentation. - Small exports in `pkg/system-probe/config/` so procmgr gate derivations stay aligned with Go `adjust*` logic.

signal.title: otel-agent: support standalone DDOT without a datadog exporter
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? - Keeps `standaloneAgentFxOptions` in the fx graph in standalone mode (`DD_OTEL_STANDALONE=true`) even when no datadog exporter is configured, so a standalone DDOT can run with e.g. an OTLP-only exporter forwarding to a gateway collector. - Adds e2e coverage: a standalone otel-agent DaemonSet leaf (dogtel extension, OTLP exporter) forwarding traces/metrics/logs to a separate Helm-deployed gateway otel-agent, which ships them to fakeintake. Also verifies the dogtel liveness metric and tagger server on the leaf, and that neither side of the topology runs a core Datadog Agent pod. ### Motivation Today, `getDDExporterConfig` returns `ErrNoDDExporter` and previously prevented standalone DDOT from starting at all when the OTel Collector config has no `datadog` exporter block (e.g. a pure leaf-to-gateway OTLP topology). This PR allows that mode to run. Related: [OTAGENT-1083](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1083) **Note on API keys in this mode:** when there is no `datadog` exporter in the config, the sync from the OTel Collector's `exporters.datadog.api.key`/`.api.site` into the agent config (`cmd/otel-agent/config/agent_config.go`, `getDDExporterConfig`) never runs, since that code path returns early on `ErrNoDDExporter`. Any component that still needs an API key in this mode (e.g. the agent serializer for the dogtel liveness metric) must instead get it the same way a regular core Agent does: via the `DD_API_KEY` env var or `api_key:` in the core config file (`--core-config`), which is loaded unconditionally, independent of the OTel Collector config. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/otel/otel-agent` — 0 issues - `TestDogtelStandaloneGateway` e2e suite run on a local kind cluster: verifies traces/metrics/logs reach fakeintake through the leaf -> gateway path, the dogtel liveness metric and tagger server on the leaf, and that no core Agent pod runs on either side. ### Additional Notes [OTAGENT-1083]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1083?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

[ ] Integration: wait for SVLS-9607 (EPRW decoder) and verify rows appear in `serverless_init_agent` REDAPL table [SVLS-9607]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9607?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [SVLS-9604]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9604?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: Fix ksm gvk collision
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a GroupVersionKind (GVK) collision in the Cluster Agent's kube-state-metrics (KSM) custom-resource collection. When two CRDs share the same `Kind` and plural name but belong to different API groups (e.g. `Project`/`projects` in both `artifactory.example.com` and `sonarqube.example.com`), they no longer collide onto a single API client. The KSM custom-resource client map was keyed by the bare plural name (`factory.Name()`, e.g. `"projects"`), which is group-blind. Two same-plural CRDs overwrote each other in the map, so both collectors' reflectors ended up sharing a single dynamic client bound to one group. The reflector for the other group then received objects of an unexpected GVK. Clients are now keyed by their fully-qualified GroupVersionResource on both the populate side (`discoverCustomResources` / `GetCustomResourceClientsAndCollectors`) and the lookup side (`getCustomResourceClient`), via a shared `CustomResourceClientKey` helper. This mirrors upstream KSM's own `CreateCustomResourceClients` keying. ### Motivation Customer escalation [CONS-8512](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONS-8512): a customer collecting custom-resource metrics for two `Project` CRDs in different API groups saw repeated `Unexpected watch event object gvk` errors in the Cluster Agent and incorrect, cross-contaminated project counts. Renaming a CRD is the only current workaround, which the customer cannot adopt. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Manual testing: I deployed a single leader Cluster Agent built from this branch into a minikube cluster with two intentionally-colliding CRDs — same Kind: Project and plural projects, but different API groups (artifactory.example.com and sonarqube.example.com) — and pointed the KSM core check at both. With the fix in place, each group's metrics stay cleanly separated: kube_customresource_artifactory_project_size reports exactly its two projects (sizes 10 and 20) and kube_customresource_sonarqube_project_size reports exactly its three (sizes 1, 2, 3), every series carrying the correct customresource_group tag with no cross-group contamination. I confirmed this both via datadog-cluster agent check kubernetes_state_core and over the wire in fakeintake, and there were zero Unexpected watch event object gvk errors in the Cluster Agent logs. - Added unit tests in `pkg/kubestatemetrics/builder/gvk_collision_test.go`: ### Additional Notes - Agent-side only — no changes to the vendored/forked kube-state-metrics. - The populate and lookup sides both route through `util.GVRFromType(f.Name(), f.ExpectedType())`, so their keys are guaranteed to agree. Falls back to the plural name when a GVR cannot be derived, matching upstream KSM behavior. - Related upstream issue (separate manifestation in the standalone KSM binary): kubernetes/kube-state-metrics#2015. [CONS-8512]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONS-8512?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: test(ssi): e2e tests for SSI Instrumentation Rules via Remote Config
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Expands `TestSSISuite/TestRemoteConfig` so APM_POLICIES is exercised end-to-end against three workloads (helm target, annotated lib-injection, unannotated) and three RC documents: - **Host-only policy** does not match Kubernetes admission facts: annotated pod stays `k8s_lib_injection`, unannotated stays uninjected, helm target still gets SSI (`applied-target=python-apps`). - **Namespace policy** (`NAMESPACE_NAME=other`) enables SSI outside the helm target, including true on-demand on the unannotated pod (`applied-policy` set). Helm fallback is unchanged. - **Deny policy** matching `targeted-namespace` overrides the local helm target (no injection, no `applied-target`). Namespace `other` is unchanged. Cluster-agent RC on the published chart is enabled via `remoteInstrumentation.enabled` (temporary until [helm-charts#2868](https://github.com/DataDog/helm-charts/pull/2868)). Extra cluster-agent env uses `envDict` so fakeintake RC settings are not replaced. Stacked on #55019. ### Motivation Catch the SSI false-positive (host-only RC flipping annotated pods), prove on-demand SSI from RC, and prove remote-before-local override — none of which unit tests cover through fakeintake + admission. ### Describe how you validated your changes - [x] Local kind-local: `dda inv new-e2e-tests.run --targets=./tests/ssi --run='TestSSISuite/TestRemoteConfig'` - [ ] CI `new-e2e-ssi` job ### Additional Notes `remoteInstrumentation.enabled` is only the published-chart RC gate, not the feature under test. Drop it once helm-charts#2868 is released.
signal.author: iamluc

signal.title: Also stop the coverage job from thrashing Bazel analysis cache
signal.text: ### Motivation "Bazel analysis cache thrashing on `main` (containerized job)" keeps alerting after #54963 ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1963914110)): all 49 occurrences of the last 24 hours come from `bazel:coverage:linux-amd64`, which now flips `cover_format`, `--collect_code_coverage` and `--instrumentation_filter`. The last one `bazel coverage` derives from the target patterns, some 400 package regexes that a post-test command cannot replay. ### What does this PR do? Skip `test2json` and UTOF where their `bazel run` cannot match the test invocation, which is only the coverage job: its tests are a **subset** of `bazel:test:linux-amd64`, still reporting them, while its JUnit tar needs no Bazel and its coverage profile only `bazel info`, which analyzes nothing. Guard the remaining `bazel run` with `--noallow_analysis_cache_discard`, turning a future divergence into a failure of the job that introduces it, rather than a warning nobody reads until a monitor fires hours later on `main` pipelines. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv bazel.process-test-results --result-json=` runs no Bazel and still packages JUnit, while a non-empty one keeps converting logs. With the server left in the coverage configuration, the guarded command exits 2 on "analysis cache would have been discarded", and stays silent after `bazel test --config=gorace`. ### Additional Notes The guard is safe for the four `bazel:test:*` jobs: `INSTALL_DIR` and `AGENT_FLAVOR` are set by packaging jobs only, so `omnibazel_flags` injects nothing there, and neither monitor has reported a flip in those jobs since #54963.

signal.title: APM: Enable convert-traces feature by default (take 2)
signal.text: This is attempt 2 due to needing to revert last version Additionally, there was a missing change in the original edits that caused the config value to not be used by serverless or OTLP receiving. This has been resolved so the PR correctly moves to convert-traces being enabled by default for all paths. To validate those changes, a number of e2e and integration tests were also updated to understand and assert on the new v1 format. ## Summary - Flips the trace-agent's `convert-traces` v1.0 payload-conversion path to be **enabled by default**. - Introduces a new opt-out feature flag, `disable-convert-traces`, for teams/customers who need to revert to the legacy code path. - Updates `pkg/trace/api/api_test.go` to reflect the new default (removes the test-only force-enable of `convert-traces`; the "without conversion" test now sets `disable-convert-traces` instead of clearing the whole `Features` map). - Update serverless use cases to also affect v1 paths (e.g. modify span, discard span) The long term plan here is to deprecate and remove the non-V1 paths. This code change adds some duplicated code for the serverless v1 span usage, but the plan is to remove the old path entirely after we have confidence with customers running the conversion logic and no issues found. ## Test plan - [x] `dda inv trace-agent.build` succeeds - [x] `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/api/...` — all 584 tests pass - [x] We have been dogfooding this conversion logic in staging and production across ALL DCs - [x] APM System-tests pass with conversion logic enabled - [ ] **TODO** Manually trigger APM system-tests to validate on all tracers

signal.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded by a single gate: **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. Every `unshare` call is reported once that gate opens, so all 12 exposed `CLONE_*` constants are matchable and the `flags` field carries the full raw bitmask. An earlier revision also filtered kernel-side on `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. That was dropped in review: it silently made rules on the other exposed constants (`CLONE_NEWUTS`, `CLONE_NEWIPC`, `CLONE_NEWTIME`, …) unable to fire. Per-flag volume control belongs in `unshare` approvers, as a follow-up. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of the gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signal.title: [SVLS-9526] Enhance startup diagnostics and surface image version
signal.text: ## Summary Stacks on #54537. When `DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`, emit a structured block at startup covering everything needed to debug serverless-init across all cloud platforms: - **`serverless_init_version`** — Docker image tag injected at build time via `-ldflags` (`pkg/serverless/tags.currentExtensionVersion`). Makes the 1:1 mapping between image tag and agent version explicit in logs. - **`deployment_model`** — `sidecar` or `init-container` - **`wrapped_command`** — the command serverless-init is wrapping, if any - **`uuid (agent)`** — the gopsutil UUID that `inventoryagent` sends to Subotka, with a direct REDAPL query hint - **Inventory pipeline section** — `first_run_delay`, `min/max interval`, `enable_metadata_collection` — confirms `ForceCollect()` preconditions at a glance - **Env var block** — all env vars (secrets masked) for platform debugging ## Changes - `cmd/serverless-init/mode/mode.go` — add `DeploymentModel` + `WrappedCommand` fields to `Conf` - `cmd/serverless-init/diagnostic/diagnostic.go` — new package with structured startup log block - `cmd/serverless-init/diagnostic/diagnostic_test.go` — unit tests ## Test plan - [ ] Set `DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`, trigger cold start — confirm all fields appear in logs - [ ] Confirm `serverless_init_version` reads `xxx` for branch builds (overridden to real tag by `serverless-init-ci` ldflags) - [ ] `dda inv test --targets=./cmd/serverless-init/...`

signal.title: fix(remoteagentregistry): canonicalize local metric help
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes Core Agent telemetry HELP text canonical when Remote Agent Registry (RAR) merges incoming Prometheus telemetry. The telemetry component records HELP text for metric families it creates in the normal `/telemetry` registry. When RAR receives a remote family with the same name, it uses that local HELP text when constructing the forwarded Prometheus descriptor. Remote-only families retain the remote agent's HELP text. ### Motivation Prometheus requires metric families that share a name to use identical HELP text. A remote agent can currently supply a different description for a metric also emitted by Core Agent, causing the combined telemetry gather to fail. The Core Agent definition is the authoritative local contract. This includes the Core Agent DogStatsD client byte counters added in #54381. The regression coverage verifies that Core Agent's `dogstatsd_client__bytes_sent` HELP wins over incompatible ADP text while retaining the ADP sample and authoritative `emitter` label. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/telemetry/impl:impl_test //comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl:impl_test --test_output=errors` - `git diff --check` - Independent spec-compliance and code-quality reviews. `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` and `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` were blocked before compilation by an internal dependency-mirror HTTP 403 for `github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/extension/healthcheckextension@v0.158.0`, which is in its mirror cooldown window. ### Additional Notes The canonical HELP catalog deliberately covers metrics created through the telemetry component's counter, gauge, and histogram factory APIs. It excludes `DefaultMetric` and opaque direct `RegisterCollector` registrations, which are not part of RAR's normal telemetry registry merge path.

signal.title: [ACTP] package and activate par-control
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Packages and activates split-mode PAR on Linux and Windows hosts: - installs `par-control` and process-manager definitions for it and the on-demand executor; - adds Agent package, installer, and Windows executable-resource wiring; - preserves a standard Unix service `PATH` for process-manager children; - adds fake-OPMS support plus Linux and Windows lifecycle/bootstrap E2E suites and CI jobs. Two details about how the definitions delegate to `dd-procmgrd`: - Windows has no console for a service to inherit, so the `par-control` definition redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `<ETC_ROOT>/logs/par-control.log` instead of the binary managing its own log file. `dd-procmgrd` now creates a missing stdio parent directory rather than silently falling back to inherit on a fresh install. - The PAR definitions set `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR=${DD_CONF_DIR}/managed/datadog-agent/stable`, which `dd-procmgrd` expands from the supervising unit, so a stable or experiment unit selects the matching config tree. Hardcoding the rendered stable path would have made the control plane and executor read stable policies during an experiment while the core Agent read the experiment's. This matches what the DDOT definition already does. Windows keeps reading `fleet_policies_dir` from the registry, as `pkg/config/setup/config_windows.go` does, because there are no experiment services there. Docker and Kubernetes deployments remain monolithic. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages:packages_test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:tmpl_test //pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test` - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/privateactionrunner` The installer test now pins the full `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` value for both definitions; asserting only the key name would not catch a regression to a hardcoded path. Live Linux and Windows E2E execution is left to CI. _Stack 9 of 9; based on #54594._

signal.title: ci: make apt mirror config resilient to slow mirrors across agent images
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes CI Docker builds resilient to slow public package mirrors, across every image in this repo that installs packages from a public host — each fitted to its own package system. **Ubuntu (apt)** (`agent`, `base-image`, `cluster-agent`, `otel-agent`, `ddot-ebpf`, podman e2e resource): apt's `mirror` method can't fail over off a *slow* mirror (only a fully-unreachable one). The base image version is configurable (`BASE_IMAGE_UBUNTU_VERSION`), so we handle **both** apt source formats: - **deb822 `ubuntu.sources` (≥ 24.04):** rewrite the `URIs:` fields to an ordered multi-URI list so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - **legacy one-line `/etc/apt/sources.list` (< 24.04):** the format can't list multiple URIs per entry, so use `mirror+file` with a peer mirrorlist (fallback on an unreachable mirror). In both paths `us-east-1` is dropped (chronically slow in every timeout log), ordering `us-west-2` → `archive.ubuntu.com` → `mirror.leaseweb.net`, and `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout turns a slow mirror into a fast error. **Debian (apt)** (`test/fakeintake`, golang base): rewrite `debian.sources` `URIs:` to Debian's AWS/CloudFront mirror `cdn-aws.deb.debian.org` first, `deb.debian.org` fallback, + Acquire timeout/Retries. (Debian has no EC2 archive mirror like Ubuntu.) **Alpine (apk)** (`Dockerfiles/dogstatsd/alpine`, `test/fakeintake` deploy stage): list `dl-cdn` primary + `mirror.clarkson.edu` secondary (apk fails over in listed order), and add the global `apk --timeout` so a slow mirror fails fast. ### Motivation `docker_build_host_profiler_standalone_amd64` was timing out (~30m, across many branches). Its `release` stage builds on `agent-base-image` (= `Dockerfiles/agent/Dockerfile`), whose `apt-get` stalled against a congested `us-east-1`. An earlier attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** stop it: job `1965243524` showed apt sticking to the slow `us-east-1` and retrying the same URI to the job timeout, even though `us-west-2` served ~90 packages in one second when apt picked it. The `mirror` method has no per-request failover on slowness — hence the deb822 multi-URI switch. Review feedback on the first pass flagged that a deb822-only rewrite regressed pre-24.04 builds (the version is configurable, and one otel build uses 20.04, which has no `ubuntu.sources`). This PR therefore handles the legacy `sources.list` too, so no build silently loses mirror coverage. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs pinpointed the stall inside the apt step of the agent-base-image release stage on a slow `us-east-1`, and showed `us-west-2` healthy. - Validated the Ubuntu and Debian `sed` rewrites against the default noble `ubuntu.sources` / focal `sources.list` / trixie `debian.sources` (GNU sed semantics), and `bash -n` on the RUN body. - Confirmed `apk --timeout` is a valid global flag (must precede the subcommand). - CI will exercise the real builds here. ### Additional Notes Local dev-tooling Dockerfiles (`tools/gdb`, `tools/ebpf/*-agent-dev`) are excluded — they don't run under `CI=true` and aren't in any CI build path. `agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` was fixed separately in the already-merged quick-fix PR (#55108). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: fix(windows): don't fail uninstall when config directory or registry state is missing
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the Windows `UninstallUser` MSI custom action so a missing registry install-state or config directory (`C:\ProgramData\Datadog` by default) no longer fails the whole uninstall. Splits `UninstallUser` into file-access and LSA-secret-removal steps so LSA cleanup always runs, guards against an unresolvable `DDAGENTUSER_NAME` operating on a bogus SID, and skips (rather than throws on) resetting base permissions when the config directory doesn't exist, while still resetting them when it does. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2107 If the registry key and/or config directory are removed out-of-band before uninstalling, the old code would throw uncaught when the directory was gone, failing the custom action entirely. ### Describe how you validated your changes `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall` already covers this: it deletes the registry key that persists `APPLICATIONDATADIRECTORY`, so uninstall falls back to the default `C:\ProgramData\Datadog`, which doesn't exist on that alt-dir install — reproducing the missing-directory failure this PR fixes.
signal.author: clarkb7

signal.title: refactor(fleet): make procmgr an independent Linux service manager
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes `procmgr` (`dd-procmgrd`) a first-class Linux service manager in the fleet installer, peer to systemd / upstart / sysvinit, instead of a systemd sub-unit that the installer cannot reason about. - New `service.ProcmgrType`, selected when the init system is systemd, `dd-procmgrd` is installed, and the operator has not opted out. New `pkg/fleet/installer/packages/service/procmgr` package whose unit-level verbs delegate to `systemd`, so no `ProcmgrType` branch calls `systemd.*` directly. - `agentService` gains a flat `Procmgr*` field group mirroring the existing `Upstart*`/`Sysvinit*` pairs, and every service-manager `switch` gains a `case service.ProcmgrType:`. `SystemdUnits*` drops `datadog-agent-procmgr.service`, so `systemd` means plain systemd again. - **Two generated unit trees**: `tmpl/gen/{systemd,procmgr}/<flavor>/`, each with its own `Wants=`. This is what makes the managers independent at the artifact level, and it replaces the `ConditionPathExists=!.../processes.d/datadog-agent-ddot.yaml` gate that had a systemd unit inspecting procmgr's state directory. New `embedded.GetProcmgrUnit` / `GetProcmgrConfig`. - The DDOT extension hooks stop touching procmgr configs entirely, and `writeDDOTProcmgrConfig`/`removeDDOTProcmgrConfig` are deleted. Process definitions are shipped unconditionally from `ProcmgrProcesses*`, exactly like units: `condition_path_exists` decides whether the payload runs, the same way `ConditionPathExists=` does for `datadog-agent-security.service`. ### Motivation From the installer's point of view procmgr was invisible: `agentService.SystemdUnitsStable` listed both `datadog-agent-ddot.service` and `datadog-agent-procmgr.service`, `datadog-agent.service` wanted both supervision paths, and mutual exclusion lived in a unit-file condition. The DDOT `processes.d` config was written from `postInstallDatadogAgent` outside the abstraction — and *not* written by `postStartExperiment`/`postPromoteExperiment`, which relied on the extension hook firing indirectly. That combination made classic-systemd/procmgr interactions hard to reason about and left no way to opt out on Linux. ### Describe how you validated your changes New tests, aimed at the invariants this design rests on: - `SystemdUnits*` contains no `-procmgr` unit and `ProcmgrUnits*` no `-ddot` unit; every name in each array resolves in its own generated tree for all four flavors (both write paths hard-fail on a missing embed, so drift would otherwise surface only at install time). - The generated `datadog-agent.service` `Wants=` matches the tree's array — the guarantee that replaced the deleted `ConditionPathExists=!` gate. - `procmgrInstallRoot` matches `DD_PM_CONFIG_DIR` in the generated procmgr units, for every package type and lifecycle half. This spans a Go helper and a generated unit, and nothing enforced it before; verified by injecting drift and confirming the test fails. Manual review of the generated trees: procmgr tree only defines datadog-agent.service with the specific Wants= sub-service that includes procmgr.service and excludes ddot.service. The yaml processes configuration are generated outside the platform scope: does depend on the platform only the package.
signal.author: Stanislas167

signal.title: feat(windows): enforce the config root security check on uninstall too
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stacked on #55136. Extends that PR's config-root owner check to uninstall and upgrade-removal, which it currently skips, and trusts one more owner: - `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` now runs unconditionally in the MSI's `InstallExecuteSequence`, including on uninstall and removal for an upgrade, instead of being skipped there. It only asserts ownership and never changes anything, so it can't leave a partial uninstall behind. - `DDCreateFolders` now runs on every install/upgrade/repair/uninstall pass instead of only on first install, creating the config root if it's missing. It only resets an existing directory's permissions on a true first install, so upgrade/repair/uninstall never strips access (e.g. ddagentuser's) granted after the directory was first created. - The maintenance dialog's config-root check is now a single check on the Welcome dialog's `Next`, covering Change, Repair, and Remove alike, instead of a separate per-button check that skipped Remove. - `ContainerAdministrator` (the account Windows containers run as by default) is trusted alongside `Administrators`/`SYSTEM` in both the Go and MSI checks. ### Motivation Uninstall-time steps that depend on the config root (e.g. the fleet installer's `prerm` hook) should get the same defense-in-depth guarantee installation already has, instead of only install/upgrade/repair being covered. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New/updated `SecureDirectory` unit tests for the create-if-missing-without-reset behavior used outside first install, and for trusting `ContainerAdministrator`. - Fixed a race in `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall`: the test deleted the Agent's registry key while the service was still running, which could let the running Agent (as `ddagentuser`) recreate the default config directory itself before the fix stopped the service first.

signal.title: [BUG] Cluster Agent External Metrics Provider returns HTTP 500 for "no serie found" — should return 422 to enable downstream FillValue/fallback handling
signal.text: ### Agent version 7.75.0 ### Bug Report When a DatadogMetric query returns no data (e.g., no matching timeseries exist for the queried time window), the Cluster Agent's External Metrics Provider wraps the error as HTTP 500 Internal Server Error via apierr.NewInternalError(). This makes it impossible for downstream consumers (KEDA, custom HPA controllers) to distinguish between "no data available for this query" and "the server is broken." KEDA (since v2.19.0) added support for metricUnavailableValue (FillValue) when the external metrics API returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. However, because the Cluster Agent always returns HTTP 500, this feature is completely non-functional when using the Cluster Agent scaler. **Possible root cause in code**: 1. When a query returns no series, queryDatadogExternal() in [pkg/util/kubernetes/autoscalers/datadogexternal.go](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/pkg/util/kubernetes/autoscalers/datadogexternal.go#L194) marks the point as invalid with error: `no serie was found for this query in API Response, check Cluster Agent logs for QueryIndex errors` 2. This sets DatadogMetricInternal.Valid = false and DatadogMetricInternal.Error = <above message> 3. When KEDA (or any HPA controller) calls GetExternalMetric(), [ToExternalMetricFormat](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/pkg/clusteragent/autoscaling/externalmetrics/model/datadogmetricinternal.go#L268-L271) returns this error because Valid == false 4. [GetExternalMetric](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/pkg/clusteragent/autoscaling/externalmetrics/provider.go#L131-L134) then unconditionally wraps all errors with apierr.NewInternalError(err), which always produces HTTP 500: `convErr := apierr.NewInternalError(err) if convErr != nil { err = convErr }` **Expected behavior**: "No data available" errors should return HTTP 422 (Unprocessable Entity) — consistent with how the Datadog API itself responds to queries with no matching data. Server errors (auth failures, connectivity issues, etc.) should remain HTTP 500. This would allow KEDA's metricUnavailableValue / FillValue to work correctly, and would be consistent with the Datadog API's own behavior. **Related upstream issues**: - KEDA [#7246](https://github.com/kedacore/keda/issues/7246) — discusses this exact Cluster Agent → 500 wrapping problem - KEDA [#7384](https://github.com/kedacore/keda/pull/7384) — added 422 FillValue handling (works for direct API, but not Cluster Agent) ### Reproduction Steps 1. Deploy Datadog Cluster Agent with external metrics provider enabled 2. Create a **DatadogMetric** with a query that returns no data: ``` apiVersion: datadoghq.com/v1alpha1 kind: DatadogMetric metadata: name: test-metric namespace: default spec: query: "sum:trace.some.metric{env:test,resource_name:nonexistent*}.as_rate()" ``` 3. Create a KEDA ScaledObject referencing this metric with **metricUnavailableValue**: ``` triggers: - type: datadog metadata: useClusterAgent: "true" datadogMetric: "default-test-metric" targetValue: "5" metricUnavailableValue: "2" ``` 4. Observe that the DatadogMetric enters error state: ``` $ kubectl get datadogmetric test-metric -o jsonpath='{.status}' # Shows: Error condition "Unable to fetch data from Datadog" # Message: "no serie was found for this query..." ``` 5. Check KEDA operator logs: ``` $ kubectl logs -n keda deploy/keda-operator | grep -i "error\|500\|fillvalue" # Shows HTTP 500 errors, no FillValue usage ``` 6. **Expected**: KEDA should receive HTTP 422, recognize it as "no data," and use the configured metricUnavailableValue (2) as the metric value 7. **Actual**: KEDA receives HTTP 500, treats it as a server error, activates fallback mechanism, and metricUnavailableValue is never used ### Agent configuration KEDA operator logs: `error getting metric value: error getting metric value (status 500): Internal error occurred: Processing data from API failed, reason: no serie was found for this query in API Response, check Cluster Agent logs for QueryIndex errors, query was: sum:trace.envoy.proxy.hits{***_env:***-sbx-2,resource_name:test*}.as_rate()` **DatadogMetric CRD status** (from kubectl get datadogmetric): Error condition: "Unable to fetch data from Datadog" Message: "no serie was found for this query" Last valid value: 13.2 (cached from 2026-02-16) Conditions: Valid=False, Active=True, Error=True ### Operating System _No response_ ### Other environment details _No response_

signal.title: fix(cws): add the mnt_namespace.ns offset when reading a mount namespace ID
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the missing `offsetof(struct mnt_namespace, ns)` term when `hook_switch_task_namespaces` reads a mount namespace ID, and extracts the read into a shared `get_mnt_namespace_inum()` helper so the two call sites can no longer disagree on how to reach the field. ### Motivation `hook_switch_task_namespaces` read `ns_common.inum` directly off the `mnt_namespace` pointer: ```c bpf_probe_read(&inum, sizeof(inum), (void *)mnt_ns + get_ns_common_inum_offset()); ``` `struct mnt_namespace` only embeds `ns` at offset 0 from Linux 5.11 onwards. Below that it sits behind `mnt_namespace.count`, so `mnt_namespace_ns` is 8 — it is 8 for all 3225 pre-BTF entries in `constants_amd64.json` below 5.11, 0 for the 28 5.11 entries, and `fallback.go` defaults it to 8. With `ns_common_inum_offset` at 16 the read therefore landed on `ns_common.ops`, i.e. the low half of the global `&mntns_operations` pointer: non-zero, stable, plausible-looking, and identical for every mount namespace on the host. The other reader of the same struct has always done it correctly, which is what made the divergence easy to miss: ```c // get_mount_mount_ns_inum bpf_probe_read(&inum, sizeof(inum), mnt_ns + get_mnt_namespace_ns() + get_ns_common_inum_offset()); ``` Consequences on affected kernels: - `process.mntns` and its copies (`exec.mntns`, `exit.mntns`, `process.ancestors.mntns`, `process.parent.mntns`, and the `ptrace.tracee` / `signal.target` / `setrlimit.target` variants) report a constant unrelated value. - `insertEntry` feeds the same value to `mountResolver.SetPidMntNs`, so mount and file path resolution can be keyed on a bogus namespace ID. The blast radius is narrower than it looks but lands on the interesting population: `mntns_cache` is only ever written by this hook, so only tasks that actually called `setns`/`unshare` and their descendants get an entry — which in practice means container workloads under runc/containerd. Everything else stays 0 and falls back to the correct procfs read in `resolver_ebpf.go`. Introduced in #45673, which added the block with the missing term. `get_mnt_namespace_ns()` already existed at that point (#42101). #54587 later renamed the accessor and fixed a different instance of the same class of bug on the netns side for Linux 7.0, but did not touch this term. ### Describe how you validated your changes | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `bazel build //pkg/security/ebpf/...` | 20 targets, build completed successfully | No new test here. The regression test is `TestSetNS/join-own-mntns` in #55126, which asserts the reported mount namespace against the inode of `/proc/self/ns/mnt`. That assertion fails on every pre-5.11 kernel in `vmconfig-security-agent.json` (amazon 4.14/5.4/5.10, centos 7.9/8, debian 9/10/11, oracle 7.9, rocky 8.4/8.5, suse 12.5, opensuse 15.3, ubuntu 16.04/18.04/20.04 — roughly half the matrix) without this fix, and passes with it. Nothing in `pkg/security/tests` asserted a mount namespace value before #55126, which is why this survived from February. ### Additional Notes **This needs to merge before #55126.** #55126 cannot go green on the older half of the KMT matrix until this lands, since its own new test is what catches the bug. Worth a backport decision: the fix changes `process.mntns` behaviour on all supported branches, and the mount-resolver impact is a functional bug rather than a cosmetic one. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: [ABLD-461] [ABLD-528] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags.
signal.text: [ABLD-461] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags. ### What does this PR do? - remove `target_compatible_with = [linux]` on //pkg/epbf. This means a lot of test targets which were silently skipped on other platforms now try to build. - Switch some network and bpf code to hand build select() clauses. - This allows us to make the dependencies match what is actually needed based on the sources which get complied for each tag. - it makes it explicit that ebpf is only used on linux - converts //pkg/network/... to dd_agent_go_test because now that we are trying those tests, we actually need the gotags. - The important outcome: This allows agent to build for macos!!! ### Motivation This unblocks building the agent on all platforms which is a high priority goal, as that unblocks the rest of Q3 work on packaging and security. The alternative is to find and remove every target_compatible_with=linux setting on a transitive dependent of //cmd/agent:agent. To do that - we would have to change every test which might depend on this from go_test to dd_agent_go_test - and probably figure out which ones need explicit linux_bpf tags added, but this adds a new config, wasting CI time - and it is less efficient than just having a smaller build graph. ### Describe how you validated your changes Build and run it on macos. ``` $ bazel run //cmd/agent:agent -- version ... Target //cmd/agent:agent up-to-date: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent INFO: Elapsed time: 7.941s, Critical Path: 7.17s INFO: Running command line: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent <args omitted> Agent 7.83.0-localbuild - Commit: dev - Serialization version: v5.0.205 - Go version: go1.26.5 ``` ### Additional Notes We should remove `--skip_incompatible_explicit_targets` from the global bazelrc. It allowed us to accumulate tech debt by making things that *appeared* to be sound but were silently just not building. Now that we are at the end of the migration, we need to surface the unfinished work. signal.title: [AAD-6] Unify detector point windows
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > 1. This is mostly for metrics that arrive every 15s, I'm thinking about how to properly manage logs that are every 1s in a future PR (instead of a 30m retention they have 2m retention this way) -> [comment](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024#discussion_r3802840340). > 2. The end goal is to unify storage when we do the warmup, some values are duplicated (future PR). This unifies all detectors (except RRCF) with an interface to get the min / max number of points per series. This way there is no discrepancy with the storage max retention (now deduced by default [1]). Warmup lazy behavior: Max retention behavior [2]: Detectors follow these conditions: 1. A new series has < min points -> no detector state created (discarded) 2. A new series has min points -> create initial state 3. The series has > min and < max points -> process + can trigger anomalies 4. The series has < min points now but had before > min points -> process (update state only if needed) but don't trigger anomalies 5. Internal detector states have max MaxPoints state points (we don't have a state for a point not present in the storage) 6. A new series can't have > max points nor > max state points (eviction) It improves memory / CPU since series that have few points don't have state, it's lazy computation. It's a tradeoff but it makes more sense to not save the states of points that are stale. Extra changes: - Bocpd has less points: (120, 200) -> (60, 120) - Added all the min / max points to the config Benchmark (all detectors enabled): Overall metric | Baseline | Changed | Delta -- | -- | -- | -- In-use heap, average | 261.02 MB | 135.29 MB | **-48.16%** Detector-phase time, average | 10.751 s | 9.835 s | **-8.52%** Macro F1 | 0.265206 | 0.267651 | +0.92% Macro precision | 0.332990 | 0.491846 | +47.70% Macro recall | 0.578832 | 0.511810 | -11.58% Predictions | 682 | 420 | -38.42% ### Motivation Memory / cpu optimization + unify detectors ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes [1] The max retention time is based on 15s / point -> `15 * max(detectors.MaxPoints) + 16` seconds [2] This is enforced by the retention time deduced by the max points for each detector so storage is always big enough We need to fine tune again to improve the scores (all detectors enabled): Scenario | F1 baseline → changed | Detector phase | Heap -- | -- | -- | -- block-building-outage | 0.285714 → 0.000000 | 22.3 → 9.7 ms | 194.7 → 39.2 MB byzantine-fault-cascade | 0 → 0 | 128.815 → 117.926 s | 1216.5 → 1219.1 MB cascading-regional-outage | 0.063224 → 0.000000 | 9.2 → 5.4 ms | 165.7 → 29.3 MB cassandra-repair-degradation | 0.318046 → 0.641981 | 48.2 → 19.5 ms | 294.8 → 62.6 MB dns-upstream-outage | 0.052606 → 0.025667 | 14.0 → 6.5 ms | 182.9 → 46.3 MB kafka-partition-saturation | 0.117641 → 0.108369 | 32.8 → 20.4 ms | 248.4 → 55.1 MB lock-contention-cascade | 0.971969 → 0.365964 | 8.9 → 3.6 ms | 141.5 → 45.4 MB memcached-eviction-storm | 0.057796 → 0.115670 | 13.5 → 4.2 ms | 129.6 → 26.8 MB pool-exhaustion | 0.093612 → 0.097034 | 9.2 → 5.5 ms | 119.1 → 15.9 MB redis-billing-latency | 0.604642 → 0.928561 | 17.6 → 9.4 ms | 185.9 → 32.6 MB redis-cpu-saturation | 0.615742 → 0.928561 | 13.7 → 5.6 ms | 147.2 → 32.6 MB tiered-cascading-outage | 0.001476 → 0.000000 | 10.1 → 3.7 ms | 106.0 → 18.6 MB

signal.title: [CWS] kmt: run x86 security-agent tests on z1d.metal
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Switches the x86_64 KMT jobs for the security-agent component from `m5d.metal` to `z1d.metal`. All five occurrences in `.gitlab/test/kernel_matrix_testing/security_agent.yml` move together: the setup job passes the type to Pulumi via `INSTANCE_TYPE_ARG`, while the upload and cleanup jobs use it as an EC2 `describe-instances` tag filter to find the host (`RESOURCE_TAGS` tags it with `instance-type:${INSTANCE_TYPE}`), so a partial change would leave those jobs waiting for an instance that never matches. arm64 stays on `m6gd.metal`, system-probe stays on `r5d.metal`, and the local-stack default in `tasks/kernel_matrix_testing/stacks.py` is untouched. ### Motivation Experiment to see whether a higher-frequency instance is a better fit for the CWS KMT matrix. | | m5d.metal (before) | z1d.metal (after) | |---|---|---| | vCPUs | 96 | 48 | | Memory | 384 GiB | 384 GiB | | Instance store | 4x900 GB NVMe | 2x900 GB NVMe | | Sustained all-core clock | 3.1 GHz base | 4.0 GHz | | On-demand, us-east-1 | ~\$5.42/h | ~\$4.46/h | Memory is unchanged, so the per-VM sizing (`--memory=12288` in `.kmt_setup_env`) needs no retuning and the guest ramfs headroom is unaffected. Local NVMe is still present, so any dependency the KMT AMI has on instance-store devices is preserved. The trade is CPU: the x86 matrix boots roughly 75 microVMs at 4 vCPUs each, so oversubscription goes from about 3x to about 6x, against roughly 15-25% more per-thread performance. Whether that is a net win depends on how CPU-bound the CWS suites actually are, which is what this PR is meant to measure. ### Describe how you validated your changes Not yet validated — draft. Plan: - [ ] Trigger `kmt_setup_env_secagent_x64` manually and confirm the instance comes up and that the upload/cleanup jobs resolve its IP through the tag filter. - [ ] Confirm the pinned KMT AMI is happy with two ephemeral NVMe devices instead of four (`lsblk` and `df -h /home/kernel-version-testing` on the live host). - [ ] Compare wall-clock of the `kmt_run_secagent_tests_x64*` jobs against a recent main pipeline. - [ ] Check for insufficient-capacity errors: z1d is an older family and the KMT subnet is pinned to a single AZ. ### Additional Notes If the CPU contention turns out to be the limiting factor, the alternative worth trying is `m6id.metal` (128 vCPUs, 512 GiB, 4x1425 GB NVMe, 3.5 GHz all-core turbo), which improves on `m5d.metal` in every dimension rather than trading cores for clock, at a higher hourly cost. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: [AGENT-16762] fix(ipc): bound local TLS handshakes
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Bounds TCP dialing and TLS handshakes for the shared Agent IPC HTTP client. This prevents loopback sockets from remaining established when a foreign service accepts a connection but never completes the TLS handshake. The Unix-socket transport clone inherits the TLS limit, and the trace telemetry and status expvar calls now use the configured IPC request timeout. ### Motivation On Windows, repeated IPC probes to an unrelated service occupying a configured loopback port could retain one socket per unsuccessful TLS handshake until ephemeral ports were exhausted. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Added a hermetic loopback regression test that consumes the TLS ClientHello and never responds. It verifies that the IPC request returns, the peer observes the socket close, and no TLS client-handshake goroutine remains parked. - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/ipc/httphelpers/... --no-cache` - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/trace-telemetry/impl/...,./comp/trace/status/impl/... --no-cache` - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/ipc/httphelpers,./comp/trace-telemetry/impl,./comp/trace/status/impl` - `dda inv linter.rst-releasenotes --files=releasenotes/notes/ipc-tls-handshake-timeout-a3a341f36dd007bb.yaml` ### Additional Notes Fixes AGENT-16762.

signal.title: [CWS] Go pprof-label span-context reader + legacy TLS removal
signal.text: ### What Swap the CWS legacy proprietary TLS APM-correlation path for a Go pprof-label span-context reader, on top of the thread-context groundwork. - **Remove legacy TLS**: `fill_span_context_legacy`, the `span_tls` map/struct, its eRPC registration, and the ebpfless ptracer span reader. `fill_span_context` is kept as the dispatch stub. - **Add tail-calls after hooks**: fill_span_context is growing and is inlined in almost every hook. Setup tail-calls after as many hooks to avoid this blowup. - **Add Go pprof reader** (`span_go.h`, `go_labels.go`): reads dd-trace-go's goroutine pprof labels by walking TLS → runtime.g → runtime.m → curg → labels, using per-process offsets resolved from the Go binary. Labels are parsed lazily in userspace to both reduce code blowup and processing time in eBPF. - **Misc**: tolerate a missing login UID (ENOENT); drive the procfs resolver test with a spawned child. ### Testing Functional tests `TestGoSpan` and `TestDDTraceGoSpan` pass.

signal.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._

signal.title: fix(rtloader): do not crash when formatting lone-surrogate Python exceptions
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a crash in rtloader when formatting a Python check exception whose message or traceback contains a Unicode lone surrogate (for example `\ud800`). `_fetchPythonError()` in `rtloader/three/three.cpp` converted traceback and exception strings with strict `as_string()`. Lone surrogates cannot be encoded as UTF-8, so conversion returned `NULL`, and appending that to a `std::string` caused a SIGSEGV in the core Agent process. This PR: - Adds `as_string_lossy()` in `rtloader/common/stringutils.c`, which encodes Unicode with UTF-8 `backslashreplace` for diagnostic paths. - Routes all exception formatting in `_fetchPythonError()` through a safe helper that skips on allocation failure. - Adds rtloader regression tests for lone-surrogate exceptions in `run_check` and `discover_config`. Strict `as_string()` behavior is unchanged for tags, metrics, events, and other hot paths. ### Motivation Reported by the rtloader vuln audit (`agent-vuln-hunt`, finding `rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-crash`). A Python integration can raise an exception whose text embeds monitored-service data containing a lone surrogate (for example JSON `{"statusstring":"\ud800"}`). That should surface as a check error, but instead crashed the entire Agent on every scheduled run. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test` - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test --test_arg=-test.run='LoneSurrogate' --test_output=all` New tests: - `TestRunCheckLoneSurrogateException` - `TestDiscoverConfigRaisesLoneSurrogate` Both assert the Agent gets a Python error containing `\ud800` instead of crashing. ### Additional Notes - Release note: `releasenotes/notes/rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-78250a6675432d3a.yaml` (`fixes`) - This closes the reported availability issue only. Other `as_string()` call sites already handle `NULL` without crashing and they may still drop or reject unencodable strings on non-exception paths.

signal.title: Add Windows `powershell` check
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a new Windows `powershell` check that runs admin-allowlisted, read-only PowerShell cmdlets and maps their output objects to metrics and tags. The data model mirrors the WMI check — `metrics`, `tag_by`, `tags`, `filters`, and `tag_queries` (joins) — so each cmdlet output object is a "row" and its properties are "columns." Key pieces: - **Config** (`config.go`): per-instance YAML parsing with dual positional-tuple / mapping forms; supports a "virtual" metric (constant value, tags carry the signal) for all-string cmdlet output. - **Allowlist** (`allowlist.go`): admin-owned policy read from the fixed, ACL-protected path `C:\ProgramData\Datadog\protected\powershell_allowlist.yaml`, constraining cmdlets, parameters, and values. Fails closed if the file is missing, malformed, or not owned by an administrator. - **Command generation** (`command.go`): parameter values are bound to the cmdlet as data (splatting + single-quoted literals + a runtime `Get-*` verb re-check), never interpolated, so untrusted values cannot inject PowerShell. - **Execution** (`powershell.go`): runs the cmdlet under a per-invocation timeout with a restricted environment and a capped output buffer, then maps rows to metrics and tags. Behavior refinements included: - A non-virtual metric whose property is missing or non-numeric causes `Run()` to error out (logged at error level, surfaced in `agent status`) rather than silently emitting nothing. - A negative per-instance `timeout` logs a warning and falls back to the default 30s. ### Motivation Windows Server exposes a large amount of operational data through PowerShell cmdlets that have no dedicated Datadog integration. This check lets customers point the Agent at a read-only cmdlet and turn its output into metrics and tags declaratively, with no custom code — the cmdlet analog of the WMI check. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/system/powershell` — 27/27 pass, covering config parsing (incl. timeout handling), allowlist enforcement, injection-safe command generation, and value/tag mapping. ### Additional Notes

The executor's idle tracking gains a distinct activity counter for this, so non-action work suppresses idle exit while `ActiveActions` still reports only running actions; - action dispatch and terminal outcomes; - Unix-socket and Windows named-pipe transports using the Agent IPC certificate; - message limits sized for large action payloads. signal.title: fix(e2e): flush fakeintake between flare suite tests (FLREM-153)
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `BeforeTest` override to `baseFlareSuite` (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/flare_common_test.go`) that flushes the fakeintake before each test, following the "one fakeintake per suite" convention documented in `test/new-e2e/AGENTS.md`. ### Motivation In e2e tests each test suite has its own fakeintake. Any test within a test suite uses the same fakeintake instance. `BeforeTest` fakeintake flush ensures that a test starts with an empty fakeintake, with no flares. `TestFlareDefaultFiles` has been flaking with `"Could not find diagnose.log file in flare archive"` (tracked in [FLREM-153](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153)). The suite never reset the fakeintake between tests, so `GetLatestFlare()` — which just returns `payloads[len(payloads)-1]` — could pick up a flare left over from a previous test, or from the framework's post-failure diagnose-flare upload, instead of the one just requested by the current test. FLREM-153 also covers a second, unrelated flake (`TestLocalFlareDefaultFiles` hitting `context deadline exceeded` on the flare POST, due to the agent's hardcoded 60s HTTP client timeout combined with infra slowness). That one isn't addressed here — see the ticket comment for details. ### Describe how you validated your changes Traced the mechanics through `test/e2e-framework/testing/e2e/suite.go` (`BaseSuite.BeforeTest`/`AfterTest`/`IsDevMode`), `test/e2e-framework/testing/environments/host.go` (post-failure diagnose flare upload), and `test/fakeintake/client/client.go` (`FlushServerAndResetAggregators`, `GetLatestFlare`) to confirm the fix addresses the root cause and matches the identical pattern already used by ~10-15 other suites in this tree. ### Additional Notes [FLREM-153]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
