signal.title: feat(notableevents): add macOS shutdown-cause notable event
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a macOS notable event that reports **why the previous boot ended**, recovered after the fact from the PMU rather than observed live. On Apple silicon, PMU/PMIC driver services publish an `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` IORegistry property: an array of short ASCII tokens naming the fault conditions that preceded the last power-off. This PR reads that property, classifies the tokens, and emits one notable event per boot when the classification is a fault. Five fault classes are covered, spanning the whole dictionary of 80 known tokens — 59 of which are faults: | Class | Title | Tokens | Example families | | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | | `thermal` | macOS overheated shutdown | 14 | `ot`, `sochot`, `ntc_shdn` | | `power` | macOS power fault shutdown | 29 | `uv`, `ov`, `oc`, `buck`, `pgood` | | `crash` | macOS crash shutdown | 6 | `crash` | | `watchdog` | macOS watchdog timeout shutdown | 5 | `timeout` | | `hardware` | macOS hardware fault shutdown | 5 | `spmi`, `sgpio`, `fault`, `otp_crc` | - **Native reader** (`shutdown_cause_iokit_darwin.{c,h}`) walks the IOService plane, flattens every `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` array into a single `0x1f`-separated token sequence, and dedups as it writes — so no Core Foundation type crosses the cgo boundary. The whole plane is walked rather than matching a class because the publishing class is PMIC-specific and varies by Mac model, and IOKit cannot match on a property key alone (`kIOPropertyMatchKey` matches key *and* value). - **Classifier** (`shutdown_classify_darwin.go`) maps a token to its *family* (prefix before the first comma, a declared underscore family, or the whole token) and the family to one of five classes, resolved by fixed precedence: **thermal → power → crash → watchdog → hardware**. Thermal wins deliberately: a machine collapsing from heat also asserts reset, crash and power lines, and the event that matters most must not be titled as a crash. - **Event shape** (`format_darwin.go`) — `EventType` is the constant `"System shutdown fault"` so consumers can filter shutdown causes on one value; the class varies the title and message only. The payload reports every token observed *plus* the families and the fault subset the classifier acted on, so a reader sees both the raw evidence and what the verdict was based on: ```json "macos_shutdown_cause": { "source": "IOPMUBootFaultInfo", "classification": "thermal", "primary_family": "ot", "families": ["ot", "sochot"], "tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "fault_tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "boot_uuid": "…", "boot_time": "2026-08-11T09:55:21Z" } ``` - **Dedup is boot-scoped.** Identity is `shutdown:<bootUUID>:<sortedFaultTokens>`, hashed under a new `macos-shutdown-v1:` event-ID prefix. Both halves are load-bearing: the boot UUID alone says nothing about *what* was read, and the token set alone is identical across boots — a Mac that overheats every afternoon would emit one ID forever and be deduplicated into silence. Tokens are sorted first because PMU enumeration order is not stable (measured: two triggers with an identical fault set reported the groups in different order). - **Storage.** A new `ShutdownCause` bookmark field records the examined boot *whether or not* an event was emitted, so a cleanly-rebooting Mac does not re-read the property on every Agent restart. It is the primary guard rather than the `Acknowledged` map, which prunes after 30 days or 4096 entries — a Mac up longer than that would otherwise re-emit. The check runs **once per collector lifetime**, before the first directory scan, and is retried from the reconcile tick when it could not commit. It reads the property as an ordinary user (no root needed; system-probe runs as root regardless), and the whole feature is gated behind the existing `notable_events.enabled` setting, which defaults to `false`. **No benchmarks, deliberately.** There is no steady-state cost to measure: the IOService walk happens once per collector lifetime, is bounded at 16 services, and short-circuits as soon as every distinct token is accounted for. It is not on any per-event, per-scan or per-tick path. **Bookmark schema version stays at 1, deliberately.** `Load()` and `validateDarwinBookmarkState()` both require exact equality, so bumping to `2` would fail every existing v1 bookmark as corrupt — which resets state and re-baselines, discarding pending undelivered crash events on every upgraded host. `ShutdownCause` is `omitempty` with a nil zero value, so v1 bookmarks deserialize with no migration. Relatedly, `types.IsEventID()` had to learn the new prefix in the same change: a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID written under the old single-prefix check would fail validation on the next `Load()` and wipe the bookmark, silently losing every pending crash event. ### Motivation [https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040) **A hard shutdown kills the Agent before it can report why.** Whether the machine overheated, lost a power rail, asserted its CRASH line, tripped a watchdog or hit a hardware fault, the Agent is gone before it can say so — the cause has to be recovered from the PMU on the next boot, or it is never recovered at all. All five fault classes are in scope here; thermal is one of them, not the point of the feature. **Predecessor: macOS app crash notable events (#54084).** This builds directly on it, reusing its bookmark, its `Pending`/`Ack` delivery contract and its at-least-once semantics unchanged — a second event *source* on that pipeline, not a second pipeline. It complements rather than replaces it: #54084 reports `.ips` files, which are written by a *running* OS about a *running* process, so a PMU-forced power cut leaves no `.ips` at all. The one adjacent artifact that does exist, `.shutdownStall` spindumps, records a *stalled* shutdown, not its cause. Everything else was surveyed and rejected: `pmset -g log` carries no cause data (25,117 lines grepped, nothing), `nvram -p` has no shutdown-cause variable, `ioreg -rc IOPMrootDomain` has no such property, `last -x reboot` is empty, and the `AppleSMC: Previous shutdown cause: <N>` unified-log line that Intel Macs emit **does not exist on Apple silicon**. Without this, a machine that overheated or lost a power rail badly enough to be cut off is a silent gap in the fleet record. `kern.shutdownreason` is **deliberately not read** — not as a source, not as a fallback, not as payload. It is the same PMU data flattened into an 80-byte-capped string, and it was already destroying data on an ordinary clean shutdown of the test machine: the cap was hit in 4 of 6 measured boots, always cutting *mid-token* and synthesising fault names that do not exist (`crash,crash`, `btn_rst,btn`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_d`). Absence of a token from that sysctl carries no information at all. The tradeoff is accepted and known: the sysctl also carries application-processor tokens (`ap_restart`, `ap_panic`) that `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not, and this PR gives those up rather than add a second parsing path and a second failure mode. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests — 240 tests pass in `pkg/notableevents`** (verified locally on the branch head with `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/notableevents/...`). Classifier tests deliberately use **payloads measured from real hardware** as fixtures rather than invented ones: | Pattern | Tokens (distinct union) | Emits | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | A — clean shutdown | `target_off_restart`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | B — `sudo reboot` | `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | C — button/force restart | + `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `crash,crash0_in` | `crash`, `fault_tokens = ["crash,crash0_in"]` | Also covered: the full 80-token dictionary maps to exactly one family each with the asserted **59 fault / 21 benign** split (14 thermal, 29 power, 6 crash, 5 watchdog, 5 hardware) — this pins a typo in the family map that would otherwise silently misclassify; class precedence in every pairing; unknown *suffix* within a known family (`ot,some_future_sensor`) still classifies thermal, which is the prefix contract; permuted group order yields an identical event ID; benign-token exclusions are dead-weight-free (each is in the measured dictionary *and* would otherwise be a fault); every classification fits the wire limit; malformed and oversized payloads are rejected. Collector tests cover the delivery contract end to end: one event per boot; `Start()` → `Close()` → `Start()` yields one event, not two; same boot UUID after Ack yields nothing; a *different* boot UUID with the same tokens yields a new event; a saturated pending queue **defers** rather than records, because recording the boot would be final and the fault cannot be reproduced by a later boot; a `Save` failure leaves nothing pending and is retried; a check blocked by an in-flight bookmark commit is retried from the reconcile tick rather than stranded for the process lifetime; reader failure, absent property and untrusted payload all leave crash-report collection unaffected; a v1 bookmark with no `shutdown_cause` key loads without being treated as corrupt. **Manual QA on real hardware.** `Mac17,9` / M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), SIP enabled, no `boot-args`. **Six real boot sessions** executed one trigger at a time — the property is destroyed by the next reboot, so the runs could not be batched — with an immediate capture script per boot: `sudo reboot`, Control-Command-Power force restart, power button held ~10s, a deliberately stalled shutdown ended by the power button, the same stall resolved via Try Again → Force Quit, and a battery run-down. Three distinct payloads were observed across six distinct boot UUIDs, verified byte-identical by MD5, reverting to pattern A after a clean shutdown. That establishes the load-bearing premise: **the property is a live, event-driven, self-clearing signal, not a constant** — which is what validates both the read path and the boot-UUID dedup key. **How to reproduce a fault event yourself — the `crash` class, on demand.** One fault class is reproducible at will on Apple silicon, so a reviewer can exercise the whole path end to end without waiting for real hardware trouble. A force restart asserts the AP's CRASH line, which emits `crash,crash0_in`: 1. Enable the feature — it is off by default: ```bash # datadog.yaml notable_events: enabled: true ``` 2. Clear any prior bookmark so the check is not skipped as already-examined, and note that the file is root-owned: ```bash sudo rm -f /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json ``` 3. Record the current boot identity and the pre-restart payload, for comparison: ```bash sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo ``` 4. Force restart: hold **Control-Command-Power** until the screen blanks. (Holding the power button ~10s, or ending a stalled shutdown with the power button, both produce the same payload — see the resolution caveat in Additional Notes.) 5. After the machine boots, confirm the PMU now reports the crash token. Expect pattern C — `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `target_off_restart`, `crash,crash0_in`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert`: ```bash ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid # must differ from step 3 ``` 6. Start the Agent and system-probe, and confirm the event: ```bash sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.agent sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.sysprobe sudo cat /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json | jq . ``` Expect a `shutdown_cause` object whose `boot_uuid` matches step 5, and a `pending` entry with a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID, `"event_type": "System shutdown fault"`, title `macOS crash shutdown`, `"classification": "crash"`, and `fault_tokens` of exactly `["crash,crash0_in"]` — all six tokens appear in `tokens`, but only the crash one elected the class. 7. Confirm the dedup guard: restart the Agent without rebooting. No second event should be emitted, and `shutdown_cause.boot_uuid` should be unchanged. To verify the **negative** case, `sudo reboot` instead of step 4 (pattern B) or shut down cleanly from the Apple menu (pattern A). Both must produce a `shutdown_cause` record with **no** event — a clean shutdown emitting an event is the failure mode most worth catching, since `wdog,reset_in_1` is present on every ordinary shutdown. **`qa/rc-required` — why this needs RC validation.** The classes that matter most in the field cannot be triggered on any machine we control, and cannot be simulated at all: the property is written by the PMU at power-off and is read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store. Reproducing a genuine thermal, power-rail or hardware fault means real failing hardware. Virtualized macOS runners expose no PMU, so the property is simply absent there and CI can only assert graceful degradation. What RC deployment adds is a full end-to-end test on real hardware: that the notable event is actually emitted and delivered, and that its tags and payload arrive intact. The predecessor, #54084, carried the same label for the same reason. **What was NOT validated, and cannot be:** - **No thermal token has ever been observed on this machine** — not `ot,*`, not `sochot,*`, not `ntc_shdn`. The thermal classification is inferred from token names in the PMU's own declared dictionary (published as `info-fault_name-<N>` properties on the `pmu,spmi` device-tree nodes). This is a hard limit, not a gap in the testing: there is **no native way to fake a thermal shutdown cause**. The value is produced by the PMU at power-off and exposed read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store — `sysctl -w` refuses (read-only OID), there is no user-settable IORegistry path, no `nvram` variable, and a userspace `os_log` line would not carry the right sender image. Generating real heat was out of scope. **The thermal path should not be described as verified in any customer-facing text or release note.** - **The real IOKit read on CI.** macOS VMs expose no PMU, so the property is absent and the reader returns empty. No E2E test is added; on a virtualized runner one could only assert graceful degradation, which is worth having but would not be thermal coverage. ### Additional Notes **Known tradeoff — `crash` fires on user force-restarts.** Measured, not hypothetical: `crash,crash0_in` appeared in pattern C with no panic induced. The token means the AP's CRASH line was asserted, which a hard reset satisfies, so **every user-initiated force restart on this hardware emits a `crash`-classified event.** Accepted because a force restart is itself a signal that something went wrong badly enough that the user gave up on the machine, and the alternative — treating the family as benign — silently dropped genuine AP and hypervisor crashes. Two commitments follow: the message says "followed a CRASH signal from the processor" and never claims a kernel panic; and if force restarts dominate emitted volume, the fix is to split `crash,hyp_*` from `crash,crash*_in`, not to revert the family to benign. **Fault allowlist, not benign denylist.** Under a denylist, any Mac whose clean shutdown emits an uncatalogued token would raise a shutdown-fault event on *every boot*. A permanent false positive is noticed and distrusted; a missed rare fault is not. The cost is that a genuinely new fault token on unfamiliar hardware is dropped silently — mitigated by matching on the family *prefix*, so `ot,anything_new` still classifies thermal. **Two benign per-token exceptions** (`shutdownBenignTokens`), for tokens whose family is a fault but whose meaning is not: `buck_boot_charge` (booting after the battery charged from depleted, not a regulator failure) and `timeout,dblclick_timeout` (the power-button double-click window). Both produced a user-visible fault event on a machine that had not faulted. Scoped to these two deliberately — the other `buck_*` tokens name real regulator failures. Excluding one only changes the outcome when it is the sole evidence for its class. **Graceful degradation is strictly additive** — nothing here can block `Start()` or interfere with crash-report collection. Property absent → no event, debug log. IOKit failure → no event. `kern.bootsessionuuid` unreadable → skip the whole check, since without a dedup key an event could repeat on every Agent restart. `kern.boottime` unreadable → fall back to the current time and omit `boot_time`. Event over the wire limit → drop and warn, **never truncate a fault payload**, because a truncated one would be misleading. Save-failure and saturation warnings latch so a persistent condition warns once rather than on every reconcile tick, and are kept separate so neither can silence the other. **Bounds are derived from real hardware, and shared between C and Go so they cannot drift.** `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SERVICE 88` and `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS 53` come from the largest known real payload (80-token dictionary, longest token 35 bytes) plus margin — 10% on count, 50% on length — and the Go-side `maxShutdownTokens` / `maxShutdownTokenBytes` are derived from those same macros. `DD_PMU_MAX_SERVICES` is 16, matching how few PMU-publishing services exist in practice. A service exceeding its bounds is dropped and logged rather than failing the read; an oversized token is truncated rather than dropping its whole service; the walk stops early once every distinct token is accounted for, since no remaining service can contribute one that has not been seen. **Intel Macs silently emit nothing.** `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not exist there; `readPMUBootFaultInfo` returns `errShutdownCauseUnsupported` when `runtime.GOARCH != "arm64"`. The Intel path (SMC shutdown-cause code `-81` via `log show`, which needs root) is unimplemented and unvalidated — no Intel Mac available. Apple documents none of this property: `org:apple-oss-distributions` returns zero hits for both `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` and `info-fault_name`. Provenance is the device's own ADT table, community string dumps of the `AppleD2255PMU` kext, and independent confirmation of the prefix decodings in `hack-different/apple-knowledge`. The *read mechanism*, by contrast, is entirely public API: `IOServiceMatching`, `IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorNext`, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.

signal.title: Skip full git clones on Windows package jobs
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Stop Windows MSI/zip package jobs from doing a full git clone (`GIT_DEPTH: 0`). They only needed history so `get_version()` could run `git describe --tags` inside the build container, which has no AWS credentials. Instead, download `agent-version.cache` on the runner host (after `assume-role`) and fail the job if that copy fails. The file is mounted into the container and xcopied into the buildroot, so `get_version()` reads the cache and never calls `git describe`. ### Motivation Full clones of this repo are expensive. These jobs can use the pipeline-default shallow clone once versioning comes from `setup_agent_version`'s S3 cache. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Confirmed `go_deps` already `needs: setup_agent_version`, so the cache object exists before package jobs start. - Confirmed the host `before_script` `assume-role` still runs (this change is in `script`, so it is not overwritten). - S3 copy uses the same `Invoke-Expression` + `$lastExitCode` pattern as `.upload_sbom_artifacts_windows`, because PowerShell 5 does not fail the job on a native `aws.exe` error. ### Additional Notes CI-only; no release note. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signal.text: #incident-59451 ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors, by giving apt real per-request failover: - Rewrites the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list (`us-west-2`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `mirror.leaseweb.net`) so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - Drops `us-east-1` (the chronically-slow mirror in the timeout logs). - `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error that triggers failover. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs, across many branches). The build spent its whole wall-clock in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror. A first attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** fix it: apt's `mirror` method sticks to one mirror per invocation and only fails over when it's fully unreachable, so a slow-but-reachable `us-east-1` kept timing out and `Acquire::Retries` retried the same URI to the job timeout. This PR switches to explicit ordered `URIs:` for genuine per-request failover. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs isolated mirror throughput as the only variable (successful same-commit runs finished in 16-21m). - Validated the `sed` `URIs:` rewrite against the default noble `ubuntu.sources`. - CI will exercise the real build here. ### Additional Notes The same fix is applied to the other CI Dockerfiles in #55119. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api (sigs.k8s.io/gateway-api)</summary> ### [`v1.6.1`](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/tag/v1.6.1) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/compare/v1.6.0...v1.6.1) ### v1.6.1 #### Major Changes Since v1.6.0 ##### Test & Conformance - Change the port used in `TCPRouteMultipleRoutesAttachment`. ([#​5053](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5053), [@​davidjumani](https://redirect.github.com/davidjumani)) - Respect `CleanupTestResources` for `BackendTLSPolicy`, `TCPRouteMultipleRoutesAttachment` and `UDPRouteMultipleRoutesAttachment`([#​5065](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5065), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - Fix `SetupTimeoutConfig()` not respecting defaults for `ListenerSetMustHaveCondition`, `ListenerSetListenersMustHaveConditions`, and `RequiredConsecutiveSuccesses`. ([#​5066](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5066), [@​immanuwell](https://redirect.github.com/immanuwell)) - Honour `tcpRouteMustHaveCondition` and `udpRouteMustHaveCondition` timeouts which were silently ignore. ([#​5067](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5067), [@​immanuwell](https://redirect.github.com/immanuwell)) ##### Other (Cleanup or Flake) - Fix `GatewayStaticAddresses` test flake by waiting for status.addresses to be published instead of assuming it appears atomically with Programmed. ([#​5038](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5038), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - Fix `GatewayInfrastructure` test flake by polling for generated infrastructure resources instead of assuming immediate visibility after the gateway is accepted. ([#​5047](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5047), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - Fix flaky `TCPRouteWeightedRouting` and `UDPRouteWeightedRouting` conformance tests by adding a data-plane readiness check before performing weighted routing assertions. ([#​5064](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5064), [@​arybolovlev](https://redirect.github.com/arybolovlev)) ### [`v1.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/tag/v1.6.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/compare/v1.5.1...v1.6.0) ### v1.6.0 #### Changes Since v1.5.1 ##### GEP & API Graduation - **UDPRoute & TCPRoute Graduation:** - UDPRoute has graduated to GA. We recommend using the "v1" API version with this API now. The "v1alpha2" version of this API is deprecated and will be removed in the future. ([#​4923](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4923), [@​zac-nixon](https://redirect.github.com/zac-nixon)) - TCPRoute has graduated to GA. We recommend using the "v1" API version with this API now. The "v1alpha2" version of this API is deprecated and will be removed in the future. ([#​4920](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4920), [@​zac-nixon](https://redirect.github.com/zac-nixon)) - **GEP Status Updates:** - Add GEP for the `XBackend` resource into Experimental status ([#​4488](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4488), [@​keithmattix](https://redirect.github.com/keithmattix)) - Move TCPRoute GEP to Standard ([#​4783](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4783), [@​zac-nixon](https://redirect.github.com/zac-nixon)) - Move UDPRoute GEP to Standard ([#​5030](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5030), [@​rikatz](https://redirect.github.com/rikatz)) ##### Feature - **API & Validation Enhancements:** - API validation updated for HTTPRoute retries: `retry.codes` must now be unique and `retry.attempts` must be >= 1. ([#​4907](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4907), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - Increase the number of allowed Certificate Authority references from `8` to `16`. ([#​4088](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4088), [@​root30](https://redirect.github.com/root30)) - The TLSRoute CRD validation has been adjusted to allow up to 1024 hostnames and rules per TLSRoute resource. Operators must validate kube-apiserver, etcd and Gateway controller behavior with representative manifests prior to enabling the new limit in production. ([#​4332](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4332), [@​alexanderstephan](https://redirect.github.com/alexanderstephan)) - BackendTLSPolicy now can be used in combination with other routes types. ([#​4745](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4745), [@​rikatz](https://redirect.github.com/rikatz)) - Allow the usage of up to 16 annotations on the gateway infrastructure object. ([#​4707](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4707), [@​wenisman](https://redirect.github.com/wenisman)) - **Conformance Infrastructure:** - Added conformance tests for UDPRoute (GEP-2645), a new GATEWAY-UDP conformance profile, a SupportTCPRoute feature, and a UDP/TCP echo server in echo-basic gated on UDP\_ECHO\_SERVER. ([#​4861](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4861), [@​zac-nixon](https://redirect.github.com/zac-nixon)) - Remove the `idleTimeout` field from the experimental SessionPersistence API. ([#​4771](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4771), [@​gcs278](https://redirect.github.com/gcs278)) ##### Documentation - **Migration & Site Updates:** - Migrate documentation from MkDocs to Docsy. ([#​4734](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4734), [@​iromanycheva-eng](https://redirect.github.com/iromanycheva-eng)) - The new wizard should be available at <https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/wizard>. ([#​4584](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4584), [@​bexxmodd](https://redirect.github.com/bexxmodd)) - **API Specs & Guidance Clarifications:** - Add missing apidoc for BackendTLSPolicy extended support. ([#​4828](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4828), [@​rikatz](https://redirect.github.com/rikatz)) - Add the missing `ListenersNotValid` programmed reason for listenerSets. ([#​4586](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4586), [@​davidjumani](https://redirect.github.com/davidjumani)) - Added documentation guidance recommending GRPCRoute for gRPC traffic. ([#​4513](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4513), [@​kahirokunn](https://redirect.github.com/kahirokunn)) - Clarified CORS API documentation to describe behavior based on `allowCredentials` instead of credentialed requests. ([#​4663](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4663), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - Previously, implementations were required to reject GRPCRoute and HTTPRoutes on the same hostname (however, few implementations did this). Now, implementations may optionally do this, or allow them to coincide. ([#​4598](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4598), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - Updates the documentation around the ListenerConditionConflicted condition. ([#​4659](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4659), [@​davidjumani](https://redirect.github.com/davidjumani)) - **Fixes:** - Grammar fix in docs for concepts/use cases. ([#​4798](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4798), [@​jkburges](https://redirect.github.com/jkburges)) ##### Bug or Regression - **IPv6 Support:** - Fix `GatewayFrontendClientCertificateValidationInsecureFallback`, `GatewayFrontendClientCertificateValidation`, and `GatewayFrontendInvalidDefaultClientCertificateValidation` failing on IPv6 clusters. ([#​4636](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4636), [@​zirain](https://redirect.github.com/zirain)) - Fix `GatewayFrontendInvalidDefaultClientCertificateValidation` failing on IPv6 clusters. ([#​4629](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4629), [@​zirain](https://redirect.github.com/zirain)) - **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP) Fixes:** - Fixed an issue where the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy prevented experimental CRDs from being installed at all (instead of only when standard CRDs already exist). ([#​4603](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4603), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - Fixed the safe-upgrades ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to allow upgrades of experimental CRDs. ([#​4557](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4557), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - **CRD & Schema Validation:** - Generated Gateway API CRD install manifests no longer include top-level CustomResourceDefinition status fields with invalid null values, fixing strict schema validation failures in tools such as kubeconform. ([#​4712](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4712), [@​MatteoFari](https://redirect.github.com/MatteoFari)) - Replace `omitempty` with `omitzero` for `supportedKinds` in ListenerStatus to preserve backward compatibility for controllers reconciling older Gateway API versions. ([#​4551](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4551), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - **API & Validation Fixes:** - It is disallowed to have repeated `filters` of `type` `CORS`. ([#​4639](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4639), [@​DamianSawicki](https://redirect.github.com/DamianSawicki)) - Limit HTTPRouteHTTPSListenerDetectMisdirectedRequests to h2 only. ([#​4665](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4665), [@​zirain](https://redirect.github.com/zirain)) - Make explicit call about resource names requiring to be RFC 1035 compliant. ([#​4787](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4787), [@​rikatz](https://redirect.github.com/rikatz)) - Make `referencegrant.spec` field required. ([#​4845](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4845), [@​bexxmodd](https://redirect.github.com/bexxmodd)) ##### Test & Conformance - **New Conformance Tests:** - Add conformance test `ListenerSetAllowedRoutesCrossNamespace` which verifies that a ListenerSet only allows routes in its own namespace by default. ([#​4841](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4841), [@​asauber](https://redirect.github.com/asauber)) - Added a conformance test covering the Gateway `Accepted` condition with reason `ListenersNotValid` and the Listener `Accepted` condition with reason `UnsupportedProtocol`. ([#​4807](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4807), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - Added conformance test `GatewayInvalidParametersRef` that verifies a Gateway referencing an invalid parameters is rejected. ([#​4808](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4808), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - Conformance: add ListenerSet tests for Route parentRef cases. ([#​4912](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4912), [@​asauber](https://redirect.github.com/asauber)) - **Test Machinery & Framework Updates:** - Conformance: `ExpectMirroredRequest` now starts its log window before the requests are sent, so mirrors are not missed on high-latency data planes. ([#​4952](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4952), [@​lexfrei](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei)) - The default polling interval for conformance tests has been decreased. This can be modified by the new `DefaultPollInterval`. ([#​4570](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4570), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - The gRPC conformance request helper no longer closes a caller-supplied (injected) `Options.GRPCClient`; it closes only the `DefaultClient` it creates internally. This lets implementations reuse a custom gRPC client across requests. ([#​4953](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4953), [@​lexfrei](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei)) - **Updates & Fixes to Existing Tests:** - The `conflicted=false` condition is not required anymore in the listener status for non-conflicted listeners. ([#​4642](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4642), [@​zhaohuabing](https://redirect.github.com/zhaohuabing)) - Fix TLSRoute conformance test to stop relying on self-signed certificates. ([#​4930](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4930), [@​rikatz](https://redirect.github.com/rikatz)) - Fixed MeshHTTPRoute307Redirect conformance test bug where the wrong manifest was used. ([#​4806](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4806), [@​jgreeer](https://redirect.github.com/jgreeer)) - Update Gateway version to v1 in UDP conformance test. ([#​4722](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4722), [@​cnvergence](https://redirect.github.com/cnvergence)) - Updated the TLSRoute conformance tests to allow FINs where previously RST was asserted. ([#​4615](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4615), [@​howardjohn](https://redirect.github.com/howardjohn)) - conformance: add missing gateway-api/skip-this-for-readiness annotation to invalid gateways ([#​5027](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5027), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) - The GRPCRouteWeight conformance test now sends its distribution-sampling requests through the injectable Options.GRPCClient instead of a hardcoded DefaultClient, allowing implementations that supply a custom gRPC client to run it. ([#​5004](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5004), [@​lexfrei](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei)) - The HTTPRouteRequestPercentageMirror conformance test now derives its acceptance band from the binomial standard deviation instead of a flat ±15% relative tolerance, removing sampling-variance flakes at low mirror percentages. ([#​5005](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/5005), [@​lexfrei](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei)) - Removed HTTPRoute retry tests with connection errors and backend timeouts ([#​4994](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/issues/4994), [@​snorwin](https://redirect.github.com/snorwin)) #### What's Changed - signal.title: test(e2e): add IBM MQ integration lab
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a deploy=true E2E-framework lab for the `ibm_mq` integration under `test/e2e-framework/scenarios/aws/integrations/ibm_mq`. The scenario self-provisions **IBM MQ Advanced for Developers 9.3** with a configurable number of queue managers and queues on a single amd64 RHEL 8 EC2 host, co-located with the Datadog Agent. A systemd-driven put/get load generator keeps queue depth and enqueue/dequeue metric families non-zero so the `ibm_mq` check has realistic work to do. It exposes knobs for: - queue-manager count and queues per manager - collection interval - queue selection strategy (auto-discovery / regex / explicit) - `collect_reset_queue_metrics` - metric exclusion patterns - integration and internal profiling Wiring: registered in the integrations `registry.go` + `BUILD.bazel`, and in the invoke task collection, giving the usual task surface: ``` dda inv aws.integrations.ibm-mq.{create,status,check,exec,ssh,destroy,reload-check} ``` ### Motivation Provide a reproducible, self-contained environment to investigate `ibm_mq` check CPU cost as queue-manager and queue counts scale — the check can become expensive with large queue counts and auto-discovery, and this lab makes that behavior easy to reproduce and profile in isolation. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `gofmt` clean on `registry.go` and all `ibm_mq/*.go`. - `go build ./scenarios/aws/integrations/...` in the `test/e2e-framework` module succeeds. - `dda inv aws.integrations -l` lists all `ibm-mq.*` tasks. - pre-commit hooks (shellcheck, go-fmt, copyright, python-linter, …) pass. ### Additional Notes Follows the existing integration-lab pattern (kafka, lustre, etc.). The scenario provisions billable EC2; remember to `dda inv aws.integrations.ibm-mq.destroy` when finished.

signal.text: This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [packaging](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging) | `==26.2` → `==26.3` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/packaging/26.3?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/pypi/packaging/26.3?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/pypi/packaging/26.2/26.3?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/packaging/26.2/26.3?slim=true) | --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>pypa/packaging (packaging)</summary> ### [`v26.3`](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/releases/tag/26.3) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/compare/26.2...26.3) <!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 26.3 --> ##### What's Changed ##### Features - Add a public `VersionRange` API and `SpecifierSet.to_range()`, representing the versions a specifier set accepts as an interval set that supports intersection, union, difference, complement, set relations, membership tests, and filtering. `VersionRange.to_specifier_set()` converts a range back to a `SpecifierSet` where a PEP 440 form exists. ([#​1267](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1267), [#​1270](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1270), [#​1298](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1298)) - PEP 808: accept `Metadata-Version: 2.6`. ([#​1194](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1194)) - Add a `limit` argument to `parse_tag()` for compressed tag sets. ([#​1220](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/issues/1220)) - Add a `prefer_sdist_predicate` argument to `Pylock.select()` to prefer source distributions over wheels for selected packages. ([#​1334](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1334)) - Add `pure_python_tags()` to generate the pure-Python tags for a Python version without touching the running platform. ([#​1346](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1346)) - Add `SpecifierSet.is_subset()`, `SpecifierSet.is_superset()`, and `SpecifierSet.is_disjoint()`, which compare the versions two specifier sets accept. ([#​1313](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1313)) ##### Behavior adaptations - Drop support for Python 3.8; packaging now requires Python 3.9 or later. ([#​1157](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1157)) - Prefer native `linux_*` platform tags over `manylinux` and `musllinux` tags on Linux. ([#​160](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/issues/160)) ##### Fixes for versions and specifiers - Raise `InvalidVersion` instead of `TypeError` when `Version` is given a non-string. ([#​1319](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1319)) - Raise `InvalidVersion` for non-string pre-release letters passed to `Version.from_parts`. ([#​1241](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1241)) - Fix an `AttributeError` when hashing internally trimmed versions. ([#​1242](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1242)) - Fix `SpecifierSet.is_unsatisfiable` for post-release boundary intersections. ([#​1257](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1257)) ##### Fixes for requirements and markers - Make `Requirement.__hash__` consistent with `__eq__` for trailing-zero-equivalent specifiers (e.g. `foo==1.0.0` and `foo==1.0.0.0`), so equal requirements hash equal and deduplicate in sets and dicts. ([#​1232](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1232)) - Normalize requested extra names before comparing or hashing requirements. ([#​644](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/issues/644)) - Preserve a `Requirement`'s specifier `prereleases` override across a pickle round trip. ([#​1204](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/issues/1204)) - Raise `InvalidRequirement` instead of `InvalidSpecifier` when a requirement contains an invalid specifier. ([#​1332](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1332)) - Clarify the error for post-release prefix wildcards like `==1.0.post1.*`. ([#​1299](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1299)) - Preserve quoting semantics when serializing marker values, so round-tripped markers parse back to the same marker. ([#​1213](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1213)) - Keep the parentheses of a nested group when serializing markers. ([#​1316](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1316)) - Normalize `extra` and `dependency_groups` values in nested markers at parse time. ([#​1246](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1246), [#​1310](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1310)) - Raise `UndefinedComparison` when a set-valued variable like `extras` is used outside the membership form. ([#​1265](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1265)) - Raise `UndefinedEnvironmentName` (a `KeyError` subclass) for missing environment keys during marker evaluation. ([#​1276](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1276)) - Wrap malformed string literal errors in `InvalidMarker` / `InvalidRequirement` instead of leaking a low-level error. ([#​1249](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1249)) - Reject requirements and markers with a trailing line break. ([#​1345](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1345)) ##### Fixes for metadata and licenses - Collect all `from_email` validation errors into one `ExceptionGroup` instead of raising the first. ([#​1268](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1268)) - Accept the UTF-8 charset case-insensitively in email payloads. ([#​1330](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1330)) - Reject malformed `Description-Content-Type` values. ([#​1329](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1329)) - Don't rewrite user values that contain `{field}` placeholders in error messages. ([#​1327](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1327)) - Route multipart email payloads to `unparsed` instead of asserting. ([#​1247](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1247)) - Make `InvalidMetadata` and `CyclicDependencyGroup` picklable. ([#​1328](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1328)) - Fold every line boundary `str.splitlines` recognizes when writing a header with `RFC822Message`. ([#​1356](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1356)) - Raise `InvalidLicenseExpression` for misplaced `WITH` clauses and empty `LicenseRef-` names. ([#​1266](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1266)) - Raise `InvalidLicenseExpression` instead of `KeyError` for a `LicenseRef-` with a `+` suffix. ([#​1219](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1219)) ##### Fixes for tags and filenames - Raise `InvalidTag` from `parse_tag()` for tags with the wrong number of components. ([#​1238](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1238)) - Reject empty tag components in `parse_wheel_filename()` and `parse_tag()`. ([#​1234](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1234)) - Reject an empty project name in the wheel and sdist filename parsers. ([#​1305](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1305)) - Reject wheel filenames with a trailing newline. ([#​1341](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1341)) - Reject wheel tags whose interpreter component is not an identifier. ([#​577](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/issues/577)) - `is_normalized_name` now rejects names with collapsed double hyphens like `a--b`. ([#​1230](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1230)) - Fix duplicate explicit `abi3t` tags. ([#​1245](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1245)) - Forward the `warn` argument to `generic_tags()` in `sys_tags()`. ([#​1264](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1264)) - Raise `SystemError` for an empty or malformed CPython `EXT_SUFFIX`. ([#​1271](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1271), [#​1301](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1301)) - Fix a typo in the macOS `fat3` architecture name (was `fat32`). ([#​1199](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1199)) ##### Fixes for pylock, direct URLs, and dependency groups - Percent-decode `pylock` artifact file names derived from a `url` so that local versions (e.g. a wheel with `2.12.1+cu130` encoded as `2.12.1%2Bcu130`) yield a valid file name. ([#​1314](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1314)) - Use an explicitly empty `tags` sequence in `Pylock.select()` instead of falling back to `sys_tags()`. ([#​1349](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1349)) - Fix `Pylock.select()` on Python builds that report a non-PEP 440 `python_full_version` (e.g. `3.15.0+`). ([#​1179](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1179)) - Reject TOML booleans where integers are expected in `pylock` files. ([#​1244](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1244)) - Add `PylockSelectError` to `packaging.pylock.__all__`. ([#​1202](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1202)) - Fix `DirectUrl` credential stripping for passwords containing `@`. ([#​1218](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1218)) - Parse the URL scheme case-insensitively when checking for file URLs in `direct_url`. ([#​1240](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1240)) - Require absolute file URLs for local directories in `direct_url`. ([#​1297](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1297)) - Collect `InvalidRequirement` errors while resolving dependency groups instead of leaking them. ([#​1302](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1302)) - Don't cache malformed dependency group parses. ([#​1248](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1248)) ##### Performance - Implement `Specifier` and `SpecifierSet` filtering with the new range engine. ([#​1120](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1120), [#​1259](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1259)) - Cache the default marker environment. ([#​1250](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1250)) - Cache the `_manylinux` module lookup process-wide. ([#​1254](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1254)) - Add `__slots__` to `Requirement` and the token classes. ([#​1320](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1320), [#​1258](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1258)) - Keep range caches across canonicalization, precompile the wheel project-name pattern, simplify `parse_tag()`, and skip `platform.mac_ver()` when the version and arch are given. ([#​1253](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1253), [#​1256](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1256), [#​1236](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1236), [#​1255](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1255)) ##### Documentation - Describe the validation scope of `packaging.pylock`. ([#​1339](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/packaging/pull/1339)) - Explain which `packaging.metadata` fields are validated. signal.title: feat(ssi): last-TRUE-wins SSI matching
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Unify SSI matching on a single last-TRUE-wins matcher: - **Static targets** (Helm / Operator / `datadog.yaml`) are reversed at construction so config first-wins is preserved. - **RC policies** keep wire order (catch-all first, exceptions after) and are last-TRUE-wins as-is. - Evaluation is static first, then RC, then SSI inject-all only when both are absent. A matched deny does not fall through. ``` SSI | static targets | RC | Decision off | — | none | nothing off | — | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | none | none | everything on | none | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | present | none | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else nothing on | present | policies | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else last matching policy, else nothing ``` Stacked on #55057. ### Motivation RC is already last-wins on the wire. Using the same matcher for static targets (by reversing them) avoids two matching modes. Static targeting is evaluated before RC so a remote deny cannot override an explicit local target. ### Describe how you validated your changes - [x] Unit tests: `./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/autoinstrumentation` - [ ] E2E `TestSSISuite/TestRemoteConfig` (HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny, LastMatchingRemotePolicyWins) ### Additional Notes `HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny` now expects the helm python workload to **keep** SSI when an RC deny matches `targeted-namespace`. That inverts the parent PR, where remote-before-local made the deny win.

signal.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signal.title: feat(autodiscovery): report ignored keys when AD formats are mixed
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Autodiscovery applies one check configuration format per entity — v2 (`checks`), then v1 (`check_names` + `init_configs` + `instances`), then legacy — and until now the ones that lost were dropped silently. This reports them through the errors `extractTemplatesFromMapWithV2` already collects, so they surface in `agent status` under `Configuration Errors` and as an AD annotation health issue. That function is the common entry point for pod annotations, container labels and Kubernetes service/endpoints annotations. ``` ad.datadoghq.com/server.checks takes precedence, ignoring ad.datadoghq.com/server.check_names, ad.datadoghq.com/server.init_configs, ad.datadoghq.com/server.instances: Autodiscovery only applies the check configuration with the highest priority (v2, then v1, then legacy) ``` Detection is limited to the keys that define a check: `ignore_autodiscovery_tags` and `logs` are excluded because they are read next to a v2 configuration — the former is applied on top of one when `cluster_checks.support_hybrid_ignore_ad_tags` is enabled. Following #41372, this uses the stored errors rather than a log line. ### Motivation A team on a cluster we operate followed the docs and added a v2 annotation to a workload that already had v1 ones, and their existing checks silently stopped — no warning, no log line, nothing in `agent status`. Both forms are valid Autodiscovery syntax, so nothing looked wrong at a glance, and finding the cause took a while. The precedence is intentional, but it is documented only in a code comment. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added cases for v1 next to v2 and v1 next to legacy; six existing mixed-format cases were updated. The single-format cases still assert no error, and the hybrid-mode case in `kube_services_test.go` guards the exclusion above. ### Additional Notes Users who mix formats today will see a new error in `agent status` and a new AD annotation health issue (`MEDIUM`); the applied configuration does not change. Follow-ups not included: the health issue's remediation steps, documenting the precedence rule, and reporting a standalone `check_tag_cardinality` that is dropped next to a v2 configuration.

signal.title: Reduce SNMP discovery load with batch writes and `synctest`
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Batch the subnet cache write so it happens once per completed discovery pass instead of once per discovered device: `snmpSubnet` gets a `cacheDirty` flag, and `writeCache` now writes only when dirty, guarded by a `WaitGroup` that tracks in-flight jobs. => `TestDiscoveryWritesCacheOnceAfterTheWholePass` verifies the cache is written once after a full pass rather than once per device. Make `Discovery.Stop()` wait for the in-flight pass, including any trailing write, before returning (previously "fire and forget"). => `TestDiscoveryStopWaitsForInFlightCheck` verifies `Stop` actually waits for an in-flight check to finish. Waiting on `Stop()` also surfaced two dormant bugs, previously unnoticed because nothing waited on the goroutine they blocked: 1. `DiscoveryWorkers: 0` scheduled jobs into an unconsumed channel and blocked forever: it now returns immediately after loading from cache instead of leaking a goroutine, 2. an unconditional `jobs <- job` could block forever once every worker was busy and `Stop()` fired, since nothing was left to receive it: scheduling a job now also selects on `d.stop`. => `TestDiscoveryStopCancelsPendingSchedule` verifies `Stop` no longer hangs on a job that was never picked up by a worker. Deflake formerly wallclock-sensitive tests thanks to `synctest`. The determinism and fixes let us **un-skip** `TestDiscoveryTicker`: the data race it used to hit running alongside other tests no longer reproduces. ### Motivation Initially motivated by tests exhibiting flakiness: - in CI ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1877754078/viewer#L552)): ``` Error Trace: pkg/collector/corechecks/snmp/internal/discovery/discovery_test.go:431 Error: Received unexpected error: timeout after waiting for 2s, expected at least 4 devices but 3 has been discovered Test: TestDeviceScansAreRequested ``` - on my machine: ``` Error Trace: pkg/collector/corechecks/snmp/internal/discovery/discovery_test.go:68 Error: Received unexpected error: timeout after waiting for 2s, expected at least 7 devices but 4 has been discovered Test: TestDiscovery ``` Profiling with `go tool trace -pprof=syscall` over 200 runs showed `syscall.openat` alone accounted for the large majority of all blocking-syscall time, entirely inside `checkDevice`/`createDevice`: every discovered device triggered a full synchronous rewrite of the whole cache file. Batching the writes cut total blocking-syscall time about 30x and `openat` specifically about 330x in a clean 200-run before/after comparison. ### Describe how you validated your changes - 553/553 tests pass across the `snmp` package tree in a single `-race` pass, with 0 skips (previously 1, see above), - 100 repeated `-race` runs of the discovery package alone, - `go tool trace -pprof=syscall` before/after, 200 runs of `TestDiscovery`: - total blocking time: **4.5s to 150ms**, - `syscall.openat`: **4.3s to 13ms**. ### Additional Notes - `writeCache` taking its own lock (previously it relied on a comment saying the caller must already hold it) is safe here: its only 2 call sites, both in `discoverDevices`, never hold `discDevMu` beforehand, - out of scope: a pre-existing, unrelated flakiness source in `pkg/collector/corechecks/snmp/status` (global `expvar` state leaking across repeated `-count=N` runs of the same test binary) is deferred to a follow-up PR.

signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Add a focused installer E2E on RHEL 9 that upgrades from a pre-rename agent (default `7.79.2`, shipping `datadog-agent-procmgrd.service`) to the pipeline build while mislabeling `/opt/datadog-agent/run` as `usr_t`. The test asserts that postinst logs the legacy procmgr retirement warning (`failed to retire legacy procmgr units`, `Access denied`), current units still come up (`datadog-agent-procmgr.service`, core agent services), the legacy unit is not loaded after upgrade, and `datadog-agent status` succeeds. Also adds `AssertJournalContainsSubstring` in the installer host helpers to search full journal output, including scriptlet logs. ### Motivation AGENT-16614 / AGENT-16559 / AGENT-16582 showed RPM upgrades failing during postinst when SELinux blocks systemd from stopping legacy `datadog-agent-procmgrd` units. #54172 makes that step warn-and-continue; this E2E covers the real upgrade path so we do not regress back to aborting postinst. A unit test would require counterintuitive production code changes. This scenario needs real systemd, scriptlets, and SELinux context. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Host helper package compiles locally (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host`) - E2E locally ### Additional Notes

signal.title: perf(test): move default test log level from `debug` to `info`
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Default test binaries to the `info` level rather than `debug`, in the test-only `init` of `pkg/util/log` that installs their logger. Make `comp/core/log/mock` follow that default instead of hardcoding it a second time, and have it restore the level that was actually in effect when a test ends, rather than assuming the default one. ### Motivation Every Go test binary in this repository logs at `debug`: the test-only `init` in `pkg/util/log` sets it, and `comp/core/log/mock` hardcoded it again for the 139 packages importing that mock. Once the level admits a line, it gets formatted, run through dozens of replacers of `pkg/util/scrubber` to redact credentials, then written out, through `t.Log` for the mock or stdout for the default logger. Tests that pass pay that too, `gotestsum` running `go test -json`, so none of it is dropped. Scrubbing one such line costs 15 allocations and about 7KiB. A run of `pkg/collector/corechecks/system/disk/diskv2` emits 9985 debug lines and one of `pkg/serverless/metrics` 4925, none of which survive this change. Both packages fail the 180s per-binary timeout of `tests_windows-x64`, at times ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1915978075)). ### Describe how you validated your changes Medians of 5 interleaved runs under CI's `-race` and `-covermode=atomic`: | package | before | after | | |---|---|---|---| | `pkg/collector/corechecks/system/disk/diskv2` | 23.13s | 15.50s | -33% | | `pkg/serverless/metrics` | 7.68s | 2.67s | -65% | Neither pair of distributions overlaps. The gain is ~4 times smaller on an uninstrumented build, -8% and -25%: the race detector and atomic coverage counters weigh more on an allocation-bound path than on a compute-bound one. `TestNewRestoresPreviousLogLevel` covers the restore, and fails against the assumed default. 419 tests pass across `comp/core/log` and `pkg/util/log`. ### Additional Notes `DD_LOG_LEVEL` keeps overriding the level, unchanged. A mock can put back the level but not the logger it replaced: `SetupLogger` closes whatever logger it supersedes.

signal.title: perf(ebpf): declare eBPF headers per program, enforce with a build check
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? eBPF programs used to depend on monolithic `cc_library` targets that aggregated entire header trees (`ebpf_c_headers`, `ebpf_c_network`, `security_ebpf_headers`, …). Clang was therefore handed **2939 repo-owned headers it never opened**, and touching any header in a tree invalidated every program that pulled that tree in. Three changes: 1. **A new Gazelle extension** (`bazel/rules/ebpf_c/`) generates one `cc_library` per header (296 across 13 trees) and derives the `deps` of all 53 `ebpf_prog` / `ebpf_program_suite` targets from the `#include`s of their source. These `deps` are now generated — run `bazel run //:gazelle` after adding or removing an eBPF header. 2. **A validation action per program** fails the build when a declared header is never opened, so over-declared `deps` cannot come back. It reuses the `unused_inputs_list` machinery from #54349, which also prunes those headers from the action's inputs and so avoids needless recompilation. 3. **Config-conditional headers move into the rule**, because whether clang reads them depends on flags the rule sets rather than on anything visible in the build graph: `asm_goto_workaround.h` (force-included into prebuilt programs) and `vmlinux.h` (reachable only under `-DCOMPILE_CORE`). `vmlinux.h`'s architecture variant is chosen by a `select()` on the existing `target_arch` flag via the new `//pkg/ebpf/c:hdr/vmlinux_arch` target. Over-declared header edges go from 2939 to zero enforced. The 39 remaining entries are irreducible: an `#include` behind a disabled `#ifdef` is declared but never read. Those are recorded in a new `allowed_unused` attribute on the 20 affected targets, each with a comment naming the guard — `kconfig.h` under `COMPILE_RUNTIME`, security test headers under `__BALOUM__`, two TLS headers under `#ifndef COMPILE_PREBUILT`, and `offsets.h` under `COMPILE_PREBUILT`. Entries that become used again are reported as stale, so the list cannot rot. The monolithic libraries are **kept**: Go cgo test targets across `pkg/network/protocols/*` depend on them to share struct definitions, and the `*_files` filegroups feed the runtime-compilation bundles in `pkg/ebpf/bytecode`. Only three now-dead `_COMMON_DEPS` variables were removed. ### Motivation Two wins. Correctness: nothing is declared to clang without being read, and the build now enforces that rather than relying on review. Build performance: a header change no longer invalidates every program in its tree, since each program declares only what it includes. Tradeoffs worth calling out: - **`deps` of eBPF programs and all `hdr/*` libraries are now generated.** Editing them by hand is pointless; the next Gazelle run overwrites them. Documented in `bazel/AGENTS.md`. - **Two places must stay in sync**: `ruleOwnedIncludes` in the extension and the flags `ebpf.bzl` sets. Called out in a comment on both sides. - Headers that `#include` each other share one library, because Bazel rejects the cycle that C tolerates through include guards. Exactly one such cycle exists (`protocols/http/http.h` ↔ `protocols/tls/https.h`). - Per-header libraries deliberately live in the tree's **root** package with slash-bearing names (`//pkg/network/ebpf/c:hdr/protocols/tls/tags`). Giving subdirectories their own packages would require `strip_include_prefix`, whose `_virtual_includes` paths stop matching what clang writes into its depfile, silently disabling the check. ### Describe how you validated your changes - All **53 eBPF programs build green on both `aarch64` and `x86_64`**, with the validation action passing on both. Verified the arch `select()` with `cquery`: under `--//bazel/rules/ebpf:target_arch=x86_64` only `hdr/vmlinux_6_14_0` is declared and the arm variant is absent, with zero repo-owned vmlinux residual on either architecture. - Downstream consumers build: `//pkg/ebpf/bytecode/...`, `//pkg/network/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/gpu/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/dyninst/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/collector/corechecks/ebpf/...`, `//pkg/security/ebpf/...`, plus`//bazel/rules/ebpf:cgo_godefs_tests` (7/7 pass). - New unit test `//bazel/rules/ebpf:check_unused_inputs_test` covers the checker: kernel headers ignored, unused repo header rejected, allowance honoured, stale allowance rejected. - **Regeneration tested**: deleted a generated library and replaced a program's per-header deps with the old monolith; a single `bazel run //:gazelle` restored both byte-for-byte, including cross-tree edges. Hand-written `allowed_unused` and the `# keep` on `hdr/vmlinux_arch` survived. Gazelle and buildifier are idempotent. ### Additional Notes Builds on #54349 (`perf(ebpf): prune unused compile inputs`), which added the `unused_inputs_list` clang wrapper this PR's check depends on. CI is the first run of the validation action outside my container. If a runner's default `target_arch` produces a different conditional-include set than the two I tested, it would surface as an `allowed_unused` mismatch naming the exact target and header — the residual was identical on both architectures locally, so I do not expect this.

signal.title: Group CWS functional tests by module config
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the CWS functional suite run as one `go test` pass per module config instead of one pass for everything. A test declares the static config it needs next to the test function: ```go var _ = declare(TestDNSResolver, testOpts{networkIngressEnabled: true}) ``` Declaring nothing means the default config, which covers most of the suite and shares a single pass — so ~180 call sites are untouched. A config that is only knowable at run time (a `t.TempDir()`, a `which(t, "sleep")`, a callback) is still passed to `newTestModule` directly, and `declareInlineConfig` records that the test builds its own module. Because declarations register at `init()`, the partition is computable without running a test. The suite prints it as JSON with `-list-groups`, and the KMT test runner (`test/new-e2e/system-probe/test-runner`) runs one `gotestsum` pass per group, each with its own junit/testjson suffix and `-test.timeout`. Everything degrades to today's single unfiltered pass — a suite that predates the flag, output that does not parse, or a package the job already narrows with `-test.run`/`-test.skip` (`cws_ad`, `cws_peds`, `cws_req`). ### Motivation `newTestModule` rebuilds the eBPF manager whenever a test's static config differs from the live module's, at seconds to tens of seconds per rebuild (measured 34s teardown on `amazon_6.12`, 7s on 5.15). Only ~16 distinct configs exist, but the tests using them are scattered through source order, so an isolated non-default test costs two rebuilds — switch in, switch back. `cws_host` does **43** rebuilds today; the partition predicts **33** on that job. ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes

signal.title: fix(ssi): run host SSI instrument-start/stop before Docker run
signal.text: In a stale state (ld.preload pointing to a non existent tmp injector), Docker doesn't start correctly. We should always run the SSI installer before Docker to clean/repair ld.preload file. Also always run the shutdown phase, even if the start was not successful (stop is idempotent).

signal.title: [procmgr] Supervise process-agent on Windows via dd-procmgr
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Moves Windows **process-agent** supervision to **dd-procmgr** using the same dual-mode pattern as PAR: - Fleet installer writes `processes.d/datadog-agent-process.yaml` (Privileged spawn profile) - Legacy `datadog-process-agent` SCM service is suppressed when procmgr owns process-agent - Agent startup waits on `dd-procmgr-service` before starting gated legacy children; independent services (sysprobe, security-agent, installer) start without blocking on procmgr **Stack context:** PR 4. Builds on [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) → [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) → [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. Reload lands in [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | This PR | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation We want subservices on dd-procmgr instead of SCM. Process-agent needs LocalSystem on Windows; other agent children should stay on the agent user. This PR wires the product integration once the procmgr foundation (PRs 1–3) is in place. `dd-procmgr-service` already runs as LocalSystem from [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Go unit tests for dependent Windows service startup (`dependent_services_windows_test.go`) - Go unit tests for fleet installer templates and YAML path substitution (`processmanager/...`) - New Windows E2E: process-agent supervised by procmgr, runs as LocalSystem, legacy SCM stopped ### Additional Notes - Linux process-agent stays on systemd for now. Legacy SCM service registration is not removed yet. - Process-agent `processes.d` config uses the shared `install_root` helper (same as PAR/ADP). MSI `RemoveFolderEx` handles uninstall/rollback cleanup; no per-file MSI rollback custom actions. - Includes release note `windows-process-procmgr-dual-mode-b7d2e4a1c8f03962.yaml`. - Closes/supersedes [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249) once the full stack merges.

signal.title: [APMB-24] map new ddnpm protocol classifications and report network_tracer telemetry on windows
signal.text: Agent side of APMB-24. Maps the new ddnpm protocol classifications into `ProtocolStack`, and adds a counter so we can survey which protocols Windows hosts speak. Pairs with DataDog/windows-drivers#198, which adds the driver-side classifiers. Merge that first. ### What changed - Five new `ClassificationRequest*` values plus regenerated `types_windows.go`. - `event_windows.go`: map them to `protocols.Stack{Application: ...}`. - `driver_interface.go`: new `windows.classified_flows` counter, tagged by protocol, incremented once per closed flow before the connection filter so it reflects everything the driver classified. - `tracer_windows.go`: run the network_tracer statsd reporter on Windows. The equivalent loop lives in the USM monitor, which is `linux_bpf` only, so until now none of the `datadog.network_tracer.*` metrics were reported on Windows at all. No payload, proto or backend changes: `ProtocolType_protocolRedis` and friends already exist in the pinned `agent-payload`, and the encoder in `usm_protocols.go` is platform-agnostic and already handles all five. Windows simply starts populating a field Linux has populated for years. ### Also fixes An existing off-by-one in the classification switch: it used `crq < ClassificationRequestHTTPLast`, and since `HTTPLast == HTTP_DELETE`, DELETE fell through to the no-op default while the driver's own range check uses `<=`. This only bit when no response was observed on the connection, since the response-side switch otherwise rescued it. ### Deployment note This is inert without the matching driver. An older ddnpm never emits the new values, so the five counters read zero and `ProtocolStack` goes unset, with no error. `WINDOWS_DDNPM_VERSION` in `release.json` needs bumping to a signed build containing DataDog/windows-drivers#198 before the survey produces data. ### Testing - Unit tests per protocol plus a regression case for the DELETE fix. Builds verified both with and without the `npm` tag. - Validated end to end on a Hyper-V VM against the real backend: driver -> ProtocolStack -> counter -> statsd -> Datadog, with per-protocol counts matching the generated traffic exactly (25 connections x 2 loopback flow directions = 50 per protocol). ### Known limitations - Loopback connections count twice, once per flow direction, since both endpoints are local. Inherent to NPM flow accounting on Windows, not introduced here, but it matters when reading the numbers. - Mongo `OP_REPLY` is not detected and Redis is matched more strictly than on Linux, so these counts are not directly comparable to Linux figures. See the driver PR for details.
